classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: opacity
items.description:
Optical depth measuring cumulative attenuation of electromagnetic radiation
along a specified propagation path through a medium. It uses the wavelength,
frequency, spectral band, or broadband weighting assigned to the attenuation
coefficient.
items.documentation:
Opacity is the optical depth accumulated by electromagnetic radiation along
a specified propagation path through a medium that removes radiation from
that path. It represents cumulative extinction by absorption and, when the
attenuation coefficient includes it, scattering out of the propagation path.

The opacity for a spectral selection $\chi$ along a path $\Gamma$ is defined
by integrating the matching local attenuation coefficient:

$$
\tau_\chi(\Gamma) = \int_\Gamma \alpha_\chi(s)\,ds
$$

where $\tau_\chi(\Gamma)$ is the opacity for path $\Gamma$ and spectral
selection $\chi$, $\alpha_\chi(s)$ is the local attenuation coefficient for
the same selection at path position $s$, and $ds$ is the differential path
element along $\Gamma$.

The spectral selection $\chi$ may be a wavelength, a frequency, a finite
spectral band, or a broadband weighting; $\tau_\chi$ and $\alpha_\chi$ must
use the same selection. This name denotes the accumulated path quantity for
the radiation component under consideration and does not by itself choose
one of those spectral conventions.

Opacity is not the local attenuation coefficient, a material-specific mass
attenuation coefficient, emitted radiance, or the [spectral absorptivity of
a filter](name:spectral_absorptivity_of_filter); it is the line-integrated
optical depth that governs attenuation along the path. For pure attenuation
with no emission into the path and no scattering into the path, incident
intensity $I_\chi^\mathrm{in}$ and transmitted intensity
$I_\chi^\mathrm{out}$ for the same spectral selection satisfy
$I_\chi^\mathrm{out}/I_\chi^\mathrm{in} = \exp[-\tau_\chi(\Gamma)]$, so
opacities of consecutive path segments add.

items.name: ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective velocity coefficient governing advective, non-diffusive transport
of the diamagnetic momentum component carried by ions of one specified
species and charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective vector coefficient for advective,
non-diffusive transport of the diamagnetic component of
[momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion species in a specified
charge state. It specializes [diamagnetic momentum convection
velocity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity) by resolving the
ion population and charge state.

The advective closure for the selected momentum component is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{s,\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{conv}} = p_{s,\mathrm{dia}}\,\mathbf{V}_{s,\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{s,\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the vector flux of
its diamagnetic momentum component, $p_{s,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the
corresponding momentum density, and
$\mathbf{V}_{s,\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection
velocity. The superscript denotes the advective contribution.

The coefficient applies to one charge state; it is neither summed nor
averaged over charge states. The [ion diamagnetic momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity) instead
concerns aggregate ion momentum. The [ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) is the
corresponding quantity without restriction to the diamagnetic momentum
component. No particular transport-direction projection or plasma region is
specified here.

This transport-closure coefficient is distinct from the ions' actual bulk
velocity and pressure-gradient diamagnetic drift velocity. The defined flux
excludes diffusive momentum transport and residual stress; external momentum
sources are separate terms in the momentum balance.

Sign convention: Positive when a projection of the effective transport
velocity directs advection along the chosen positive transport direction;
the sign of the corresponding momentum flux also depends on the signed
momentum density.

items.name: runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_compton_scattering
items.description:
Compton runaway-electron source rate is the volumetric rate at which
high-energy gamma-ray scattering transfers thermal electrons into the
runaway population.
items.documentation:
The Compton runaway-electron source rate describes the production of runaway
electrons through energy transfer from high-energy gamma-ray photons to
initially thermal electrons. Only scattering events that place an electron
in the runaway regime contribute, rather than all events that produce
energetic electrons.

The source contribution to the runaway-electron density evolution is defined
by

$$
S_{\mathrm C}=\left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{RE}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{Compton\ source}}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm C}$ is the Compton source rate, $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the
runaway-electron number density, and $t$ is time. The restriction denotes
the density change attributable solely to Compton production.

This term counts transfer into the runaway population, not creation of
additional electrons. It excludes other production mechanisms, particle
transport, and runaway-electron losses, and therefore is not the full
density time derivative. It contributes to the [total runaway-electron
source rate](name:total_runaway_electron_source_rate), which sums all active
production mechanisms.

No spatial averaging is imposed by this definition. The [volume-averaged
Compton runaway-electron source
rate](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_compton_scattering)
is the plasma-volume average of this quantity, not its volume integral.

items.name: toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Toroidal angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume from Coulomb
collisions to trapped thermal ions in a specified charge state, projected in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the collisional torque-density
vector delivered to trapped thermal ions in a specified ionic charge state.
It represents angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume from Coulomb
collisions with background charged species.

The toroidal projection is defined by

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{q,\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{th}}$ is the
trapped thermal ion charge-state collisional torque density, $q$ identifies
the ionic charge state, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

This quantity retains only the toroidal projection and remains resolved in
ion charge state; it excludes torque transferred to passing or other ion
populations and contributions attributed to noncollisional processes. The
charge-state-aggregated counterpart is [toroidal trapped thermal ion torque
density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: line_averaged_krypton_density
items.description:
Line-averaged krypton density is the chord-length average of the total local
krypton number density, summed over all charge states from neutral krypton
through fully stripped krypton.
items.documentation:
Line-averaged krypton density is the chord-length average of the total local
krypton number density. It includes every krypton charge state, so it
measures elemental krypton abundance along a specified line of sight rather
than the density of one particular ionization state.

For a chord parameterized by path length, the line average is defined by:

$$
\langle n_\mathrm{Kr} \rangle_\mathrm{line} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L \sum_{q=0}^{36} n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}(\ell)\,d\ell = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_\mathrm{Kr}(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $\langle n_\mathrm{Kr} \rangle_\mathrm{line}$ has units of
$\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, $L$ is the chord length in meters, $\ell$ is distance
along the chord in meters, $q$ is the integer charge-state index with $q=0$
for neutral krypton and $q=36$ for fully stripped krypton,
$n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}$ is the local density of charge state $q$ in
$\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, and $n_\mathrm{Kr}=\sum_{q=0}^{36} n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}$
is the charge-state-summed local [krypton_density](name:krypton_density).

This quantity is a normalized path mean, not an unnormalized line integral.
It differs from
[volume_averaged_krypton_density](name:volume_averaged_krypton_density),
which averages the same charge-state-summed local density over a plasma
volume rather than along a chord.

items.name: spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector
items.description:
Energy-dependent probability that a photon impacting a hard X-ray detector
is registered by its detection system.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the conditional photon-registration probability for a hard
X-ray detector at a specified photon energy. It characterizes the detector
response after a photon has impacted the detector, rather than the incident
photon flux or the geometric collection probability.

At photon energy $E$, the efficiency is defined by

$$
\epsilon(E) = \frac{N_{\mathrm{registered}}(E)}{N_{\mathrm{incident}}(E)}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{registered}}(E)$ is the number of impacting photons
registered by the detector and $N_{\mathrm{incident}}(E)$ is the number of
photons impacting it at energy $E$. The efficiency is bounded between zero
and one and is the hard-X-ray counterpart of [spectral efficiency of a soft
X-ray detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_soft_xray_detector).

items.name: vertical_plasma_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Kinematic coefficient relating vertical diffusive transport of plasma ion
momentum to the opposing vertical gradient of ion momentum density.
items.documentation:
Vertical plasma momentum diffusivity is the kinematic transport coefficient
governing vertical diffusion of [momentum](name:momentum) in the plasma ion
momentum balance. The vertical direction is parallel to the toroidal
symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is distance from that axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical position.

For a momentum component entering the ion balance, the local Fick-law
closure is:

$$
\Pi_{i,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_Z\frac{\partial g_i}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\Pi_{i,Z}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of that momentum
component through a surface normal to increasing $Z$, $g_i$ is its ion
momentum density, $D_Z$ is this vertical directional diffusivity, and the
subscript $i$ denotes the ion population represented in the balance.

The momentum density is aggregated over the ionic constituents and charge
states included in that population; the diffusivity itself is not a sum of
charge-state coefficients. Neutral-particle momentum is excluded. This
coefficient describes the gradient-driven contribution only, excluding
convective momentum transport, residual stress, and external momentum
sources. Vertical transport need not be normal to a magnetic flux surface or
parallel to the magnetic field.

Within the ion momentum balance, this coefficient supplies the vertical
directional component of [plasma momentum
diffusivity](name:plasma_momentum_diffusivity). The [vertical ion
charge-state momentum
diffusivity](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity) instead
resolves the corresponding transport coefficient for a specified ionization
state.

items.name: total_ion_energy_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective transport velocity relating the combined convective energy flux of
all ion species to their summed local transported energy density.
items.documentation:
The total-ion energy convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient
multiplying the combined ion energy density to give the combined convective
ion energy flux. It is the all-ion aggregate specialization of [ion energy
convection velocity](name:ion_energy_convection_velocity), with the
transport-coefficient meaning of [energy convection
velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity).

For nonzero total transported ion energy density, its defining relation is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{i,W}=\frac{\sum_s\mathbf{Q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}}{\sum_s\mathcal{W}_s}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{i,W}$ is the total-ion energy convection velocity, $i$
denotes ions, $W$ labels the energy transport channel, $s$ indexes ion
species and their ionic charge states, $\mathbf{Q}_{s,\mathrm{conv}}$ is
each population's convective energy flux, and $\mathcal{W}_s$ is its
transported energy density.

Both sums include all ion species and all their ionic charge states.
Electron and neutral energy contributions are excluded, as is the
gradient-driven diffusive contribution to ion energy flux. Where
population-specific convection velocities are defined using their respective
energy densities, this coefficient is their energy-density-weighted mean,
not their arithmetic sum. It need not equal the [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity).

The [parallel total-ion energy convection
velocity](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity) is the
projection of this vector along the local magnetic field; the parent
quantity is not restricted to that direction or to a particular plasma
region.

Sign convention: Positive when a projected convective ion-energy flux points
along the positive projection direction: along the local magnetic field for
a parallel projection, and outward toward the last closed flux surface for a
flux-surface-normal projection.

items.name: perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Perpendicular normalized momentum flux due to E×B drift is the dimensionless
linear-eigenmode weight for laboratory-frame toroidal angular-momentum
transport in the perpendicular velocity-space channel.
items.documentation:
Perpendicular normalized momentum flux due to E×B drift is the electrostatic
contribution to toroidal angular-momentum transport across magnetic flux
surfaces for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode in the laboratory frame. The
perpendicular label identifies the velocity-space channel relative to the
equilibrium magnetic field, not the direction of transport across the flux
surface.

For a specified eigenmode-amplitude convention, the normalized weight is
defined by

$$
\Gamma_\perp = \frac{\Pi_\perp^{\mathrm{es}}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\Gamma_\perp$ is this normalized linear weight,
$\Pi_\perp^{\mathrm{es}}$ is the perpendicular-channel contribution to
laboratory-frame toroidal angular-momentum flux carried by the fluctuating
E×B drift, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference momentum-flux
scale. The superscript $\mathrm{es}$ denotes the electrostatic contribution
driven by the perturbed electrostatic potential. Neither the reference scale
nor the eigenmode-amplitude convention is fixed by the name.

The weight applies to one linear eigenmode at its specified wavevector; it
does not imply a sum over modes or a saturated nonlinear transport level. It
represents laboratory-frame momentum transport, not rotating-frame momentum
transport.

This is the perpendicular-channel specialization of [normalized momentum
flux due to E×B
drift](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). With matching
population, mode, and normalization conventions, adding the
[parallel-channel
contribution](name:parallel_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
gives the full electrostatic toroidal momentum flux. It excludes the
separate perpendicular-channel contributions attributed to [perturbed
parallel vector
potential](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential)
and [perturbed parallel magnetic
field](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field).

items.name: electron_temperature
items.description:
Temperature of electrons expressed as two-thirds of the mean random kinetic
energy per bulk electron, excluding directed-flow energy.
items.documentation:
Temperature of electrons characterizes the random translational motion of
the bulk electron population relative to its mean flow. It is a kinetic
temperature, distinct from the equivalent blackbody temperature assigned to
emitted radiation.

The defining energy-equivalent relation is

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}}\right\rangle_e
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature, $E_{e,\mathrm{rand}}$ is an
electron's kinetic energy relative to the local mean electron flow, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_e$ denotes a particle-number-normalized average over
the bulk electron velocity distribution. For a Maxwellian population, this
equals the thermodynamic temperature expressed as an energy.

This quantity applies to electrons in the core, edge, and scrape-off layer
without imposing a particular evaluation locus or spatial averaging
convention. It excludes directed-flow kinetic energy and does not include
ion thermal energy. As a single temperature, it does not resolve separate
directional kinetic temperatures.

The [line-averaged electron
temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature) is a spatial average
of this quantity along a plasma chord, while the [volume-averaged electron
temperature](name:volume_averaged_electron_temperature) is its volume
average inside the last closed magnetic flux surface. These spatial averages
are distinct from the velocity-distribution average in the defining
relation.

items.name: hard_xray_emissivity
items.description:
Local production rate of hard-X-ray bremsstrahlung photons per plasma volume
and emission solid angle, integrated over a specified photon-energy band.
items.documentation:
Hard-X-ray emissivity is the local bremsstrahlung photon production rate per
plasma volume and emission solid angle, integrated over the selected
hard-X-ray photon-energy band. It represents emission from suprathermal
electrons at a physical location and in a specified emission direction.

The band-integrated emissivity is defined by

$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HXR}}(\mathbf{r},\Omega;E_1,E_2)=\int_{E_1}^{E_2}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HXR}}^{(E)}(\mathbf{r},\Omega,E)\,\mathrm{d}E
$$

where $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HXR}}$ is the band-integrated hard-X-ray photon
emissivity, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HXR}}^{(E)}$ is the differential photon
emissivity with respect to photon energy, $\mathbf{r}$ is the emission
location, $\Omega$ is the emission direction labeled by solid angle, $E$ is
photon energy, and $E_1$ and $E_2$ are the lower and upper limits of the
selected energy band.

This quantity is local and directional: it is not integrated along a line of
sight, over a plasma volume, or over emission directions. It applies to
hard-X-ray photons produced by suprathermal-electron bremsstrahlung and
excludes the total bremsstrahlung electromagnetic power and
detector-received radiation.

In an optically thin plasma, [hard X-ray
brightness](name:hard_xray_brightness) is obtained from the corresponding
local emissivity by propagation and integration along a viewing path;
brightness is therefore a received radiance, whereas this quantity is the
local photon source density.

items.name: fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per
plasma volume delivered to a specified fast ion charge state through Coulomb
collisions.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum source associated
with Coulomb momentum transfer to a specified fast ion charge state. Orbit
classes and directional components select particular contributions without
changing this common physical meaning.

For a selected angular-momentum direction, the torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a} = (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_a
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}$ is the torque density about direction $a$,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the rotation axis,
$\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to
the specified fast ion charge state, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the
corresponding unit vector. For toroidal angular momentum in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this relation reduces to $R f_\phi$.

This quantity is the fast-ion, charge-state-resolved realization of ion
charge-state torque density due to collisions; [co-passing fast ion
charge-state torque density due to
collisions](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
and [toroidal fast ion charge-state torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
are orbit-resolved or component-resolved instances.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected angular-momentum transfer is in
the positive orientation of its stated axis; for toroidal angular momentum,
positive is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: second_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector
items.description:
Full transverse extent of the rectangular ion-source aperture along the
neutral beam injector’s second local tangential axis, defining one aperture
dimension for beam extraction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the full geometric width of the rectangular ion-source
aperture measured along the neutral beam injector’s second local tangential
axis. It is one of the two orthogonal aperture dimensions used to define the
extraction opening.

The width is defined by the extrema of the aperture boundary coordinate:

$$
w_2 = x_{2,\rm max} - x_{2,\rm min}
$$

where $x_2$ is the [second local-tangential coordinate of the neutral beam
injector](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector),
and $x_{2,\rm max}$ and $x_{2,\rm min}$ are its maximum and minimum values
on the aperture boundary. This quantity applies to rectangular geometry and
denotes the full width, not a half-width or the orthogonal first local
tangential dimension represented by [first local tangential width of the
neutral beam
injector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector).

items.name: toroidal_vorticity
items.description:
Projection of the curl of plasma center-of-mass velocity along the toroidal
direction, measuring signed local bulk-flow rotation about that direction.
items.documentation:
Toroidal vorticity is the component of plasma [vorticity](name:vorticity)
along the geometric toroidal direction. For solid-body rotation, it is twice
the toroidal component of a fluid element's angular velocity.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the toroidal
projection is defined by:

$$
\omega_\phi = (\nabla \times \mathbf{v}) \cdot \hat{\phi} = \frac{\partial v_R}{\partial Z} - \frac{\partial v_Z}{\partial R}
$$

where $\omega_\phi$ is toroidal vorticity, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
[center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), $v_R$ and $v_Z$ are
its cylindrical radial and vertical components, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector along increasing toroidal angle, and $\nabla \times$ is the
right-handed curl operator.

The scope is the local single-fluid plasma bulk flow, without restriction to
a particular plasma region or any surface, volume, or time averaging. The
underlying velocity is the mass-weighted mean flow of the constituent plasma
species, not a species- or charge-state-resolved velocity. This quantity is
not vorticity magnitude, flow shear, strain rate, divergence, or
magnetic-field-line twist; it is also distinct from toroidal flow speed and
angular velocity.

Unlike [parallel vorticity](name:parallel_vorticity), which projects the
same curl along the local magnetic field, toroidal vorticity uses the
geometric toroidal direction independently of magnetic-field orientation.

Sign convention: Positive when the plasma-flow curl has a positive
projection along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counter-clockwise when
viewed from above the plasma.

items.name: fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density
items.description:
Fast neutral internal-state number density is the local abundance per
physical volume of nonthermal neutral particles of one species in one
specified internal state.
items.documentation:
Fast neutral internal-state number density is the local abundance per
physical volume of suprathermal neutral particles of one selected species in
one specified internal state. It counts particles rather than weighting them
by charge, mass, or energy.

The density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the fast population:

$$
n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{fast}} = \int f_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast neutral number density, $s$
labels the neutral species, and $a$ labels its internal state. The
superscript $0$ denotes electrical neutrality, and $\mathrm{fast}$
identifies the nonthermal population. The function
$f_{s,a}^{0,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the local velocity distribution of that
population, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element; the integral covers all velocity space.

No summation over species or internal states is implied. Thermal neutrals,
neutral particles in other internal states, and charged particles are
excluded. No spatial averaging or restriction to the scrape-off layer is
implied.

For the same species and internal state, [neutral internal-state
density](name:neutral_internal_state_density) is the sum of this fast
contribution and [thermal neutral internal-state
density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density). Summing this
contribution over all internal states gives the [fast neutral
density](name:fast_neutral_density) of the selected species. Combining the
fast and thermal populations across those states gives its [total neutral
number density](name:total_neutral_number_density).

items.name: current_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Electric current carried by a plasma current-carrying filament element is
the signed toroidal current assigned to a single discrete element in an
axisymmetric filamentary representation of the distributed plasma current.
items.documentation:
Electric current carried by a plasma current-carrying filament element is
the signed toroidal current assigned to one discrete element in an
axisymmetric filamentary representation of the distributed plasma current.
It represents that element's contribution to the plasma current rather than
a geometric property of the element.

For filament element $k$, the current is the cross-sectional integral of the
toroidal plasma current density over that element:

$$
I_k = \int_{A_k} j_\phi \, dA
$$

where $I_k$ is the electric current carried by plasma filament element $k$,
$A_k$ is the area of the plasma filament element in the poloidal
cross-section, $j_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the plasma current
density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $dA$ is a
differential area element of the poloidal cross-section.

The scope is one plasma current-carrying filament element, with no
aggregation over multiple elements. It applies only to plasma-current
filaments in the axisymmetric representation and excludes currents in coils,
passive conductors, and other non-plasma structures. It is an integrated
current, not a current density and not a geometric descriptor; the element
geometry is described separately by [inner
radius](name:inner_radius_of_plasma_filament),
[height](name:height_of_plasma_filament), and area.

The represented [plasma current](name:plasma_current) of a collection of
plasma current-carrying filament elements is the algebraic sum of their
signed filament currents.

Sign convention: Positive when the current of the plasma filament element
flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; this is
counter-clockwise when viewed from the positive $Z$ direction.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of helium-4 ions averaged over the full plasma-boundary flux
surface, summed over all ionic charge states and excluding neutral helium-4.
items.documentation:
Number density of helium 4

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{He4}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{He4}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{He4}}\rangle$ is the averaged helium-4 ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the local helium-4 ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

The density is summed over all positive helium-4 ion charge states and is
not a local point value, a volume average, or a density that includes
neutral helium-4. It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local
[helium-4 ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary);
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting replaces that parent quantity's
pointwise value with a surface mean. The isotope-specific scope
distinguishes it from [flux-surface-averaged helium-3 density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

Related quantities:
[flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Temperature over the scrape-off layer is the thermal plasma temperature
associated with the open-field-line edge region outside the confined plasma.
It is a parent quantity whose specializations define any species, locality,
or averaging convention.
items.documentation:
Temperature over the scrape-off layer is the scalar thermal plasma
temperature associated with particles in the scrape-off layer, the
open-field-line edge region outside the confined plasma. It denotes the
temperature concept for that region without fixing a particular plasma
species, spatial locus, or averaging measure.

This parent quantity applies only to plasma in the scrape-off layer and not
to temperatures in the closed-field-line confined plasma or to
material-surface temperatures. It also does not by itself specify whether
the represented SOL temperature is local, region-averaged,
field-line-associated, or otherwise aggregated; those semantics belong to
concrete specializations.

A specialization such as [average temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer) is a narrower
quantity that adds an averaging convention while retaining the same
scrape-off-layer temperature concept.

items.name: fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power
items.description:
Fast electron power is the total coherent-wave power absorbed by the fast
(non-thermal) electron population, integrated over the plasma volume.
items.documentation:
Fast electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power
transferred to the fast, non-thermal electron population throughout the
plasma volume. It is the fast-electron component of [electron absorbed wave
power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power).

The volume-integrated power is defined by

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_V p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-electron absorbed wave power,
$p_{e,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local coherent-wave power density
absorbed by fast electrons at position $\mathbf{x}$, and $V$ is the plasma
volume.

This quantity excludes wave power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons, ions,
and other populations, as well as wave power that is launched but not
absorbed. Unlike [fast electron power at inside flux
surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it represents the
total plasma-volume integral rather than a cumulative value inside a
specified flux surface. The population scope is complementary to [thermal
electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

items.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction
items.description:
Toroidal current density due to ion–neutral friction is the signed
electric-charge flux contribution along the toroidal direction arising from
momentum exchange between ions and neutrals.
items.documentation:
Toroidal current density due to ion–neutral friction is the toroidal
projection of the [current density due to ion–neutral
friction](name:current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction). It represents
the electric-current contribution attributable to frictional momentum
exchange between plasma ions and neutral particles.

The component is defined by

$$
j_\phi = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $j_\phi$ is this toroidal current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the ion–neutral-friction current-density
vector, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector. The direction is
defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
the distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$
is the vertical height.

This is a local contribution in a partially ionized plasma, without spatial
averaging or integration. It excludes contributions assigned to other
mechanisms and does not represent the total plasma [current
density](name:current_density). The [radial current density due to
ion–neutral
friction](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_neutral_friction) is a
different projection of the same mechanism-resolved vector, rather than an
additional mechanism.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion–neutral-friction contribution carries
conventional electric current in the direction of increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$.

items.name: ammonia_prefill_count
items.description:
Ammonia prefill count is the total amount of NH3 introduced before plasma
breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count of 10 per neutral
molecule.
items.documentation:
Ammonia prefill count is the total amount of neutral ammonia, NH3,
introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron
count. Each neutral NH3 molecule contributes ten count units: seven from
nitrogen and one from each of its three hydrogen atoms.

The count is defined by the accumulated molecular amount over the prefill
interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}} = 10N_{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} 10\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron
count, $N_{\mathrm{NH_3,prefill}}$ is the accumulated number of ammonia
molecules, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{NH_3}}$ is the ammonia injection rate in
molecules per second, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the start of
prefill and plasma-breakdown times in seconds.

This species-specific contribution is included in the common prebreakdown
bookkeeping of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count). Ammonia introduced after
breakdown is excluded and is represented by
[accumulated_ammonia_count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count).

items.name: inner_radius_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Inner radial boundary of the annular cross-section of a ferritic element in
the axisymmetric equivalent geometry, defining the bore of the annulus
centered at a reference point in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
The inner radius specifies the internal boundary of the annular
cross-section used to represent a ferritic element in the axisymmetric
thick-line equivalent geometry. Ferritic elements are ferromagnetic inserts,
and each element is represented by an axisymmetric body whose cross-section
is an annulus centered at a reference point $(R_0, Z_0)$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius from the
toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height,
$R_0$ is the major-radius coordinate of the annulus center, and $Z_0$ is its
vertical coordinate.

For an annular cross-section with inner radius $r_\mathrm{in}$ and outer
radius $r_\mathrm{out}$, the enclosed area is

$$
A = \pi\bigl(r_\mathrm{out}^2 - r_\mathrm{in}^2\bigr)
$$

where $A$ is the cross-sectional area, $r_\mathrm{in}$ is the inner radius,
and $r_\mathrm{out}$ is the [outer radius of the ferritic
element](name:outer_radius_of_ferritic_element); both radii are radial
distances from the annulus center in the cross-section. The constraint is $0
\leq r_\mathrm{in} < r_\mathrm{out}$.

This quantity applies to a single ferritic element in the axisymmetric
equivalent geometry and is not averaged or summed over multiple elements.
Together with the [outer radius of the ferritic
element](name:outer_radius_of_ferritic_element), it defines the annular
cross-section; the [radial coordinate of the ferritic
element](name:radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element) specifies the
major-radius placement of the element rather than its inner boundary.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Toroidal neutral momentum convection velocity is the toroidal projection of
the effective velocity that convects aggregate neutral momentum. The
toroidal label denotes the velocity component along increasing toroidal
angle, not the component of momentum being transported or a particular
neutral particle flow.
items.documentation:
Toroidal neutral momentum convection velocity is the toroidal component of
the effective velocity vector that advects neutral momentum in a transport
closure for the aggregate neutral population. The toroidal component is the
projection along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height; toroidal modifies the velocity component, not the momentum
component being transported. It is a convection coefficient and need not
equal the toroidal neutral velocity.

The projection defining this component is

$$
u_{\phi,\mathrm{mom}} = \mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is the [neutral momentum convection
velocity](name:neutral_momentum_convection_velocity), $\hat{\phi}$ is the
unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $u_{\phi,\mathrm{mom}}$
is this quantity.

The unqualified neutral population denotes an aggregate over neutral species
and internal states; resolved counterparts keep those populations separate.
This coefficient belongs to the convective part of the neutral momentum flux
and excludes diffusive, viscous, source, sink, and residual terms; it is not
the [toroidal neutral momentum flux](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux)
itself.

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{mom}}$ has a component
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of krypton ions, averaged over
charge states at the radial location of an internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the krypton-ion bulk flow
evaluated at the radial location assigned to the internal transport barrier.
It includes ionic krypton charge states and excludes neutral krypton.

$$
v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr}} = \\frac{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr},q}}{\\sum_q n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ionization states, $n_{\\mathrm{Kr},q}$ is the
number density of ions in state $q$, and $v_{\\phi,\\mathrm{Kr},q}$ is their
toroidal bulk-flow component. The result is the density-weighted mean over
all included krypton ionization states, analogous to the corresponding
[toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal krypton
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

The toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\\phi, Z)$ frame, where $\\phi$ increases in the toroidal direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the krypton-ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

items.name: ion_atomic_mass
items.description:
Ion atomic mass is the neutral-atom reference mass of a selected elemental
or isotopic constituent of an ion species, independent of ionic charge
state.
items.documentation:
Ion atomic mass is the reference mass assigned to one atom of a selected
constituent element or isotope in an ion species. It specifies atomic
composition using the corresponding neutral atom, including its bound
electrons, rather than the charge-dependent rest mass of the ion.

The atomic mass is related to the corresponding relative atomic mass by

$$
m_i = A_{\mathrm r,i}\,m_{\mathrm u}
$$

where $m_i$ is the neutral-atom reference mass of the selected constituent
of ion species labeled $i$, $A_{\mathrm r,i}$ is that constituent's relative
atomic mass, and $m_{\mathrm u}$ is the atomic mass constant, defined as one
twelfth of the rest mass of a free neutral carbon-12 atom in its ground
state.

The value applies per atom of the selected constituent, not to the total ion
population. For a molecular ion, it describes one constituent atom rather
than the complete molecule. It is a physical mass, not the integer nucleon
count called the mass number, a mass density, or a mass flow rate. No
restriction to thermal or fast ions is implied.

This quantity specializes [atomic mass](name:atomic_mass) to a constituent
of an ion species. It uses the same neutral-atom reference convention as
[neutral-beam atomic mass](name:neutral_beam_atomic_mass), but does not
restrict the constituent to an injected beam species.

items.name: trapped_thermal_particle_source_rate
items.description:
Trapped thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric
rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the trapped orbit class.
items.documentation:
Trapped thermal particle source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric
rate at which thermal particles enter or leave the trapped orbit class.
Trapped particles are those whose parallel velocity reverses along a
magnetic field line and therefore undergo bounce motion between mirror
points.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{n,\mathrm{in,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}-S_{n,\mathrm{out,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the trapped thermal particle
source rate, $S_{n,\mathrm{in,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local rate of
thermal particles entering the trapped orbit class,
$S_{n,\mathrm{out,tr}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local rate leaving it, $\psi$
is the magnetic-flux surface label, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes
a flux-surface average.

This quantity applies only to the thermal population and the trapped orbit
class. It is averaged over each magnetic flux surface and combines all
contributing particle source and sink processes; positive values represent
net entry into the trapped class, while negative values represent net
removal. It excludes co-passing and counter-passing particles.

It is the trapped-orbit contribution to the aggregate [thermal particle
source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), which combines the source
rates of the thermal orbit populations. It is complementary to the
[co-passing thermal particle source
rate](name:co_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate) and [counter-passing
thermal particle source
rate](name:counter_passing_thermal_particle_source_rate), which describe the
two passing orbit classes.

items.name: maximum_magnetic_field
items.description:
Largest value attained by a selected magnetic-field quantity over its
specified evaluation domain, without fixing its source, projection,
magnitude, or locus.
items.documentation:
The maximum magnetic-field quantity is the extremal value of a selected
magnetic-field quantity evaluated over a specified domain. It is a
domain-level reduction of the local [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field),
rather than the local magnetic-field vector itself.

The maximum operation can be represented abstractly as

$$
M = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{D}} Q(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $M$ is the resulting maximum magnetic-field value, $Q(\mathbf{x})$ is
the selected local magnetic-field quantity, $\mathbf{x}$ is an evaluation
point, and $\mathcal{D}$ is the specified evaluation domain.

This parent fixes the maximum aggregation over the domain but imposes no
particular magnetic-field source, physical state, projection, magnitude
selection, population, or plasma or vacuum region. The result is one
extremal value for the selected domain, not a local value, average,
integral, or mode-resolved quantity.

It is distinct from the local [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field) and does
not by itself determine whether the selected quantity is a total field,
source contribution, signed component, or field magnitude. The child
[maximum magnetic-field magnitude](name:maximum_magnetic_field_magnitude)
specializes this parent by selecting the magnitude of the total local
magnetic-field vector before applying the maximum operation.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Signed major-radius component of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion
charge state in the edge plasma, positive away from the toroidal symmetry
axis.
items.documentation:
The radial component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
signed projection along the major-radius direction. This direction points
away from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,R} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{R} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{R}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,R}$ is the radial drift component for the specified ion charge
state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$
is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and
$\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. The definition
requires a nonzero magnetic field and applies to magnetized ions; at fixed
local fields, the ideal drift is independent of ion mass and charge.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma, including the scrape-off layer; it is neither
summed nor averaged over charge states or species. Other contributions to
ion motion are excluded. It is a signed linear velocity component, not a
speed, a flux-surface-normal projection, or the magnitude of the
field-perpendicular velocity.

Together with the
[toroidal](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
and
[vertical](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
components, it resolves the parent drift vector in the cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame. Although the ideal drift is perpendicular to the magnetic
field, its major-radius projection need not vanish because the major-radius
direction is not generally field-aligned.

Sign convention: Positive when the E×B drift has a component toward
increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal component of the bulk flow velocity assigned to the effective
deuterium–tritium fuel species at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge
pedestal.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the bulk-flow velocity of deuterium and tritium treated as
one effective fuel species, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the
H-mode edge transport barrier. It is distinct from the velocity of deuterium
alone, such as [toroidal deuterium velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

The effective toroidal velocity is the mass-density-weighted mean of the
isotope flow components:

$$
v_{\mathrm{DT},\phi} = \frac{m_D n_D v_{D,\phi} + m_T n_T v_{T,\phi}}{m_D n_D + m_T n_T}
$$

where $m_D$ and $m_T$ are the deuterium and tritium masses in kg, $n_D$ and
$n_T$ are their number densities in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{D,\phi}$ and
$v_{T,\phi}$ are their toroidal velocity components in m.s$^{-1}$. The
effective species uses the deuterium–tritium fuel convention with mean
atomic mass 2.5; this local quantity is not a flux-surface average or a
value at the plasma boundary, such as [toroidal deuterium–tritium velocity
at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the velocity points in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the internal transport barrier is the ψ value on
the nested magnetic flux surface that marks the barrier location between the
magnetic axis and plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the internal transport barrier is the
poloidal-flux-function value $\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ on the nested magnetic
flux surface identified with the internal transport barrier. An internal
transport barrier is a core or mid-radius region of reduced turbulent
transport; this quantity gives the barrier location as a poloidal-flux
label, not the magnitude of the transport reduction.

The surface-value definition is

$$
\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}} = \psi(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ITB}})
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the magnetic flux surface identified
with the internal transport barrier and $\psi(\mathcal{S})$ is the [poloidal
magnetic flux at a flux
surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface) for surface
$\mathcal{S}$.

Relative to the axis and boundary references, the normalized poloidal-flux
label is $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ITB}} = (\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}} -
\psi_{\mathrm{axis}})/(\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}} - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}})$,
where $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic
axis](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis) and
$\psi_{\mathrm{boundary}}$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary). Absolute $\psi$
values include an additive reference; direct comparison of
$\psi_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ values requires the same additive reference and sign
convention, whereas flux differences and normalized labels are unchanged by
a common additive offset. This poloidal-flux location is distinct from the
[toroidal flux radius at the internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
from edge pedestal loci such as the [poloidal magnetic flux at the pedestal
top](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pedestal_top).

Sign convention: Positive when a flux surface outward from the magnetic axis
toward the plasma boundary has $\psi - \psi_{\mathrm{axis}} > 0$.

items.name: incident_ion_particle_flux_at_wall
items.description:
Areal arrival rate of particles from a selected ion species at a wall
surface, summed over all ionization states.
items.documentation:
Incident ion particle flux at a wall is the local rate at which particles
from a selected ion species arrive at a wall surface per unit area. It
counts arriving particles rather than their charge or deposited energy.

The flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_i^{\mathrm{inc}}(A,t)=\frac{\partial^2 N_i^{\mathrm{inc}}}{\partial A\,\partial t},\qquad N_i^{\mathrm{inc}}=\sum_z N_{i,z}^{\mathrm{inc}}
$$

where $\Gamma_i^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident particle flux of ion species
$i$, $A$ is wall surface area, $t$ is time, $N_i^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the
cumulative number of incident particles of species $i$, $z$ is the
ionization-state index, and $N_{i,z}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the cumulative
number arriving in state $z$.

The quantity applies locally to the selected wall surface and to the
selected ion species, with contributions summed over all of that species'
ionization states. It includes particles moving toward and reaching the
wall, but excludes emitted particles, neutral particles, other ion species,
and charge-state-resolved values.

It is the charge-state sum represented by the [ion charge-state particle
flux at the wall](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_at_wall). Unlike the
[incident ion energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:incident_ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
it counts arriving particles without weighting them by deposited or carried
energy.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_beryllium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Dimensionless beryllium abundance formed by dividing the volume-averaged
beryllium density by the volume-averaged electron density.
items.documentation:
Dimensionless beryllium abundance formed by dividing the volume-averaged
beryllium density by the volume-averaged electron density. It represents the
abundance of ionized beryllium relative to free electrons in the confined
plasma volume.

The abundance is defined by the ratio of the two volume averages:

$$
a_{\mathrm{Be}} =
\frac{\langle n_{\mathrm{Be}} \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
=
\frac{\left\langle \sum_{q=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}} \right\rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $a_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the beryllium abundance ratio, $\langle \cdot
\rangle_V$ denotes averaging over the confined plasma volume,
$n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the charge-state-summed beryllium ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in charge
state $q$, and $n_e$ is the [electron density](name:electron_density).

The numerator is the [volume-averaged beryllium
density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density), summed over all ionized
beryllium charge states and excluding neutral beryllium atoms. The
denominator is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) over the same confined
plasma volume.

This quantity is a ratio of two global volume averages, not a pointwise
impurity fraction and not the volume average of $n_{\mathrm{Be}}/n_e$. It is
not charge-weighted; a charge-weighted beryllium contribution to
quasineutrality would use terms proportional to $q n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}$
rather than the unweighted ion sum. The local pre-averaged counterpart of
the numerator is [beryllium density](name:beryllium_density).

items.name: vertical_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
items.description:
Vertical magnetic field on a control surface is the signed axial component
of the external-coil vacuum field remaining after its toroidal mean is
removed.
items.documentation:
Vertical magnetic field of the non-axisymmetric vacuum contribution is the
signed component parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis, evaluated at
individual points on a control surface. It contains only the toroidally
varying external-coil contribution to the [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined
by

$$
B_{Z,\mathrm{NA}}(R,\phi,Z)=\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{NA}}(R,\phi,Z)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}=B_{Z,\mathrm{vac}}(R,\phi,Z)-\left\langle B_{Z,\mathrm{vac}}\right\rangle_\phi(R,Z)
$$

where $B_{Z,\mathrm{NA}}$ is the vertical non-axisymmetric component,
$\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{NA}}$ is the [non-axisymmetric magnetic-field
vector](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), and $B_{Z,\mathrm{vac}}$ is
the vertical component of the external-coil vacuum field before
toroidal-mean removal. The brackets denote averaging over a complete
toroidal circuit at fixed major radius $R$ and vertical coordinate $Z$;
$\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector
parallel to the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$.

The axisymmetric vacuum contribution and fields generated by plasma currents
are excluded. Each value is a local component, not a surface average,
surface integral, or Fourier coefficient. Unlike the [normal
non-axisymmetric magnetic
field](name:normal_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), this projection follows
the fixed vertical direction rather than the local control-surface normal.

Sign convention: Positive when the non-axisymmetric vacuum magnetic field
has a component toward increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: total_ion_temperature
items.description:
Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion
population, with all species and charge states contributing according to
their number densities.
items.documentation:
The total ion temperature is the density-weighted effective temperature of
the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion
species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes
directed bulk-flow energy.

The local effective temperature is defined by

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} n_s T_s}{\sum_{s\in\mathcal{S}} n_s}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density and $T_s$ is the ion temperature of
species or charge state $s$, and $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of included
thermal ion populations. Thus, “total” denotes a density-weighted
combination, not an arithmetic sum of temperatures. Spatially transformed
instances apply line or volume averaging to this combined quantity, as in
[line_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature)
and
[volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature);
the underlying species-resolved quantity is
[ion_temperature](name:ion_temperature).

items.name: current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Electric-current-density contribution driven by plasma pressure gradients,
including the perpendicular diamagnetic current and its associated
field-aligned return current.
items.documentation:
Current density due to diamagnetic drift is the pressure-gradient-driven
contribution to [electric current density](name:current_density) in a
magnetized plasma. It includes the perpendicular diamagnetic drive and the
associated field-aligned return current, rather than denoting a projection
onto a diamagnetic direction.

In the isotropic-pressure fluid limit, its decomposition is

$$
\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}+j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}\hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic-drift current-density
vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $p$ is the total
isotropic pressure of the charged plasma populations, and $\nabla p$ is its
spatial gradient. The magnetic-field unit vector is
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, and $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}$
is the [parallel current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), defined by
$j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

The contribution is summed over charged plasma populations and is not
restricted to a particular species or to the plasma edge. It is
mechanism-resolved: projecting the total current from all mechanisms onto a
diamagnetic direction does not isolate this contribution. Independently
driven currents are excluded.

Under stationary quasineutral current closure, the associated field-aligned
return current balances the divergence of the perpendicular diamagnetic
drive. The [Pfirsch–Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
identifies the specific return-current contribution associated with toroidal
magnetic geometry; it is not the entire current-density vector.

Sign convention: Positive when a projected component represents net
positive-charge transport along its defining positive direction; the
parallel projection is positive along the local magnetic-field unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: normalized_perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude
items.description:
Normalized perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the modulus of the
complex normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation eigenfunction for a
gyrokinetic mode. It retains the phase-independent amplitude while
discarding the arbitrary complex phase.
items.documentation:
Normalized perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the modulus of the
complex normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation eigenfunction for a
gyrokinetic mode. It represents the phase-independent strength of the
electrostatic potential component of the mode and excludes the arbitrary
complex phase of the eigenfunction.

For a complex normalized perturbed electrostatic potential eigenfunction
$\delta\hat{\phi}$, the amplitude $A_{\phi_N}$ is defined by its complex
modulus:

$$
A_{\phi_N} = |\delta\hat{\phi}| = \sqrt{\left(\operatorname{Re}\delta\hat{\phi}\right)^2 + \left(\operatorname{Im}\delta\hat{\phi}\right)^2}
$$

where $\operatorname{Re}\delta\hat{\phi}$ and
$\operatorname{Im}\delta\hat{\phi}$ are the real and imaginary parts of the
same normalized eigenfunction, and $A_{\phi_N}$ is the corresponding
dimensionless amplitude.

This quantity is not the complex eigenfunction itself and contains no phase
information. Its value is non-negative and depends on the normalization
chosen for $\delta\hat{\phi}$, so it denotes relative mode structure within
that normalization rather than an independently fixed absolute scale.

items.name: radial_force_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description:
Signed radial component of the net electromagnetic Lorentz force on an
individual poloidal-field coil, resolved along increasing major radius.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the net electromagnetic force on an individual
poloidal-field coil projected onto the radial direction. It describes the
resultant coil load, not the local electromagnetic body-force density.

The radial force is defined by

$$
F_R = \int_{V_\mathrm{coil}} (\mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}\,dV
$$

where $V_\mathrm{coil}$ is the conductor volume, $\mathbf{J}$ is the
current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector,
$\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the radial unit vector, and $dV$ is the volume
element. The radial and vertical components together determine the
[electromagnetic force of a poloidal-field
coil](name:force_of_poloidal_field_coil); the corresponding vertical
component is given by the [vertical force of a poloidal-field
coil](name:vertical_force_of_poloidal_field_coil). It is distinct from
[radial volumetric force](name:radial_volumetric_force), which is a local
force density rather than a net force.

Sign convention: Positive when the force points toward increasing major
radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part
items.description:
Plasma mass density imaginary part is the imaginary quadrature of a complex
plasma mass-density quantity. It is the component multiplying the positive
imaginary basis, not the complete complex density.
items.documentation:
Plasma mass density imaginary part is the imaginary quadrature of a complex
plasma mass-density quantity. It represents the coefficient of the imaginary
basis in a complex representation of plasma mass density, not the complete
complex density itself.

The complex plasma mass density may be decomposed into real and imaginary
quadratures as

$$
\rho = \rho_{\mathrm{re}} + i\,\rho_{\mathrm{im}}
$$

where $\rho$ is the complex plasma mass density, $\rho_{\mathrm{re}}$ is its
real quadrature, $\rho_{\mathrm{im}}$ is the plasma mass density imaginary
part, and $i^2=-1$.

This parent quantity covers imaginary-part plasma mass-density fields
independent of the particular origin of the complex representation. The
[perturbed plasma mass density imaginary
part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part) is a first-order
perturbation case. It excludes the real quadrature, the complex modulus, the
phase, and the complete complex plasma mass density.

Sign convention: Positive when the quadrature coefficient is along the $+i$
direction in the complex representation of plasma mass density.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density
items.description:
Thermal ion charge-state number density is the local abundance per physical
volume of one ion species in one charge state, excluding fast and
suprathermal ions.
items.documentation:
Thermal ion charge-state number density is the local abundance per physical
volume of thermalized bulk ions of one selected species in one specified
positive charge state. It counts particles rather than weighting them by
charge, mass, or energy.

The density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the thermal population:

$$
n_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal ion number density, $s$ labels
the ion species, $q$ is its positive ionic charge number, and the
superscript $\mathrm{th}$ identifies the thermal population. The function
$f_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local thermal-ion velocity distribution,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element; the integral covers all velocity space.

No summation over species or charge states is implied. Neutral particles,
ions in other charge states, and fast or suprathermal ions are excluded. The
quantity is local, including spatial variation within a poloidal
cross-section, rather than a flux-surface or volume average.

For the same species and charge state, [ion charge-state
density](name:ion_charge_state_density) is the sum of this thermal
contribution and [fast ion charge-state
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density). Summing this thermal
contribution over all ion species and positive charge states gives the
[total thermal ion density](name:total_thermal_ion_density).

items.name: major_length_of_iron_core_segment
items.description:
Euclidean length of the alpha-side of an iron-core segment’s oblique
parallelogram cross-section in a constant-toroidal-angle poloidal plane of
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. The side is inclined relative
to the major-radius direction and the value is a non-negative distance.
items.documentation:
Euclidean length of the alpha-side of an iron-core segment’s oblique
parallelogram cross-section is the non-negative distance between the two
endpoints of that designated side. The edge lies in a constant-$\phi$
poloidal plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height;
its inclination is specified by
[alpha_angle_of_iron_core_segment](name:alpha_angle_of_iron_core_segment).

For endpoints 1 and 2 of the designated alpha-side, the length is

$$
L_\alpha = \sqrt{(R_2 - R_1)^2 + (Z_2 - Z_1)^2}
$$

where $L_\alpha$ is this alpha-side length, and $R_i$ and $Z_i$ are the
major-radius and vertical coordinates of endpoint $i$.

The quantity is the alpha-side specialization of
[length_of_iron_core_segment](name:minor_length_of_iron_core_segment). It
excludes the other parallelogram side, the full cross-sectional extent, and
[height_of_iron_core_segment](name:height_of_iron_core_segment), which
denotes a different iron-core segment dimension. Because it is a Euclidean
length, it is not a signed orientation, coordinate displacement, or vector
projection.

items.name: energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Energy flux at the wall due to surface emission is the energy carried away
per unit area and time, summed over emitted species and energy
contributions.
items.documentation:
Energy flux at the wall due to surface emission is the outward energy
transport rate per unit area associated with surface-emission processes. It
includes the kinetic energy of emitted particles and other emitted energy
contributions, rather than being restricted to radiation alone.

The local emitted energy flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_W^{\mathrm{em}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}W_{\mathrm{em}}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\Gamma_W^{\mathrm{em}}$ is the emitted energy flux density,
$W_{\mathrm{em}}$ is the energy carried away through surface emission, $A$
is wall surface area, and $t$ is time.

Contributions are summed over emitted species, their charge states, and
emitted energy channels. The quantity is local to the wall, not a
surface-integrated power or spatial maximum. It excludes incident energy and
is not the net energy deposited at the wall.

This is the energy-transport specialization of [flux at the wall due to
surface emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). Its
[kinetic-energy
contribution](name:kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission)
accounts for energy carried by emitted particle motion. The net energy flux
received by the wall equals the [incident energy
flux](name:incident_energy_flux_at_wall) minus this emitted energy flux.

Sign convention: Positive when energy is carried away from the wall into the
plasma.

items.name: methane_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous rate of neutral methane-molecule delivery into the plasma
vessel by gas injection, counted per molecule rather than as an
equivalent-electron or elemental source.
items.documentation:
Methane source rate is the instantaneous rate at which neutral methane
molecules are delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection. It counts
methane molecules directly, rather than converting them to equivalent
electrons or to elemental carbon or hydrogen.

The source rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t) = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{CH_4}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of methane molecules
delivered by gas injection and $t$ is time. The quantity is distinct from
the [methane carbon-13 source rate](name:methane_carbon_13_source_rate),
which applies specifically to carbon-13-labeled methane.

items.name: trapped_current_density
items.description:
Trapped current density is the vector density of conventional electric
charge flux associated with trapped-particle transport, including its
collisional drag back-current.
items.documentation:
Trapped current density is the vector density of conventional electric
charge flux associated with the trapped-particle contribution. It includes
direct charge transport by trapped particles and the collisional drag
back-current attributed to that contribution.

A kinetic decomposition is

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\sum_s q_s\int_{\mathcal{T}_s}\mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v+\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{drag,tr}}(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes charged species,
$q_s$ is species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the
velocity-space distribution function, $\mathcal{T}_s$ is the
trapped-particle region of velocity space, and
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{drag,tr}}$ is the associated collisional drag
back-current.

This vector contribution is a specialization of
[current_density](name:current_density), not a scalar electric current or a
particular geometric projection. toroidal_current_density supplies a
geometric projection, while
[toroidal_trapped_current_density](name:toroidal_trapped_current_density) is
the toroidal, flux-surface-averaged specialization of the trapped
contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when any stated component or scalar projection of
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is aligned with the positive direction of its
defining basis vector or unit vector.

items.name: left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part
items.description:
Signed imaginary quadrature of the left-hand circular E-plus wave
electric-field phasor along a beam or ray path, relative to a specified
phase reference.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the left-hand circularly
polarized E-plus component of a wave [electric field](name:electric_field)
phasor along its propagation path. It retains signed phase information and
is not the field amplitude or the instantaneous physical electric field.

The defining relation is:

$$
E_{+,I} = \operatorname{Im}(E_+)
$$

where $E_{+,I}$ is the signed imaginary quadrature, $E_+$ is the [left-hand
circularly polarized wave electric-field
phasor](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), and
$\operatorname{Im}$ selects its imaginary part.

The parent polarization component is transverse to the local equilibrium
magnetic field. This quadrature is evaluated locally along the beam or ray
propagation path, including electron cyclotron emission paths; it is not
integrated along that path. It inherits the circular-polarization basis and
phase reference of the parent phasor.

Together with the [left-hand circularly polarized real
part](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part), it
reconstructs the parent component through $E_+ = E_{+,R} + iE_{+,I}$, where
$E_{+,R}$ is the real, in-phase quadrature and $i$ is the imaginary unit.
Changing the phase reference mixes the two quadratures without changing the
physical polarization.

Sign convention: Positive when the E-plus phasor lies in the upper half of
the complex plane defined by the specified phase reference.

items.name: toroidal_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Toroidal component of the bulk flow velocity of the fictitious
deuterium-tritium single-species (atomic mass 2.5 amu), evaluated at the
plasma boundary (last closed flux surface).
items.documentation:
The toroidal deuterium-tritium velocity at the plasma boundary is the
$\hat{\phi}$-component of the bulk-flow velocity of a fictitious
single-species representing a deuterium-tritium fuel mixture with atomic
mass 2.5 amu, evaluated at the plasma boundary — the last closed flux
surface separating magnetically confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.

The toroidal projection is defined as:

$$
v_\phi^{DT} = \mathbf{v}_{DT} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{DT}$ is the bulk-flow velocity of the fictitious
deuterium-tritium species and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is a local point evaluation at the plasma boundary, distinct
from
toroidal_flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_tritium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary,
which gives the flux-surface mean at the same location, and from
[toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary),
which resolves the deuterium species independently rather than treating the
D-T mixture as a single effective species.

items.name: parallel_plasma_momentum_flux
items.description:
Parallel plasma momentum flux is the transfer rate per unit area of
field-aligned linear momentum across an oriented surface, summed over
charged plasma populations.
items.documentation:
Parallel plasma momentum flux is the signed rate per unit area at which the
field-aligned component of [linear momentum](name:momentum) crosses an
oriented surface. The parallel qualifier selects the transported momentum
component, not the direction normal to the surface.

It is the field-aligned projection of the [plasma momentum
flux](name:plasma_momentum_flux):

$$
\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{pl}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf F_{\mathrm{pl}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\left(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}\right)
$$

where $\Gamma_{\parallel,\mathrm{pl}}$ is this parallel momentum flux,
$\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the nonzero local magnetic field,
$\mathbf F_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the vector of plasma momentum transported per
unit area and time across the oriented surface,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma momentum-flux tensor, and
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen positive unit normal to that surface.

The quantity applies to aggregate charged-population momentum transport in
the edge plasma, summed over electrons and all ion species and ionic charge
states. It includes convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or
turbulent-stress contributions; it is not restricted to diffusive transport
and excludes neutral momentum transport. The [parallel ion charge-state
momentum flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) instead
restricts the transported momentum to one ion charge state.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transferred across the
surface in its chosen positive-normal direction is co-directed with the
local magnetic field.

items.name: thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power
items.description:
Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the total coherent-wave power
absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population, integrated over the plasma
volume.
items.documentation:
Thermal electron absorbed wave power is the plasma-volume integral of the
local coherent-wave power deposition density into the bulk thermal electron
population. It is the thermal-electron component of [electron absorbed wave
power](name:electron_absorbed_wave_power), rather than the total absorbed
power across all plasma channels.

The defining volume integral is

$$
P_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{abs},e}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the [thermal electron power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density), $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the
plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is differential
volume.

The integral includes only power absorbed by bulk thermal electrons and
excludes deposition into fast electrons, ions, and other channels. Unlike
[thermal electron power at inside flux
surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), it covers the
complete plasma volume rather than a specified enclosed region.

items.name: first_local_tangential_radius_of_filter_window
items.description:
Geometric radius describing the bending of an X-ray filter window along its
