first local tangential direction, defined for applicable curved-surface
geometries.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local radius describing how an X-ray filter-window
surface bends along its first local tangential direction.

For the surface normal section tangent to that direction, the curvature
radius is defined by:

$$
R = \frac{1}{|\kappa_1|}
$$

where $R$ is the first-local-tangential radius of curvature and $\kappa_1$
is the normal curvature along the first local tangent.

This quantity applies to an individual filter window when its curved-surface
geometry specifies bending along the first local tangent. It describes
surface shape, not aperture size, and is a radius rather than curvature
itself. No front/back surface distinction is implied.

This is a directional surface-curvature specialization of
[radius](name:radius). The [second-local-tangential
radius](name:second_local_tangential_radius_of_filter_window) describes
bending along the other local tangent; neither tangent is necessarily a
principal-curvature direction.

items.name: plasma_current
items.description:
Plasma current is the signed integral of a plasma current-density component
over a poloidal cross-section; its global equilibrium value is the net
toroidal current.
items.documentation:
Plasma current represents conventional electric charge transport carried by
the plasma, integrated over a poloidal cross-section and resolved along a
specified direction. Its global equilibrium value is the total toroidal
current through the full plasma poloidal cross-section.

The component-resolved current is defined by

$$
I_a(S) = \int_S \mathbf{j}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a\,dA
$$

where $I_a(S)$ is the integrated plasma current in direction $a$, $a$ labels
the selected component, $S$ is the selected poloidal cross-sectional region,
$\mathbf{j}$ is the total plasma [current density](name:current_density),
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the local unit vector along that component's
positive direction, and $dA$ is an unsigned area element.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is distance from the
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The
global plasma current is $I_p=I_\phi(S_p)$, where $I_p$ denotes the total
toroidal plasma current, $S_p$ is the full plasma poloidal cross-section,
and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\phi$ points toward increasing toroidal angle.

The current density includes all charged-particle contributions with their
electric-charge signs. The integral is therefore a net conventional current,
not a particle flux or a sum of unsigned current magnitudes. Currents
carried by external coils and conducting structures are excluded.

The [cumulative plasma current inside a flux
surface](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_plasma_current) restricts the
integration region to the poloidal cross-section enclosed by that surface
while retaining the specified current component. For the toroidal component,
it equals the global plasma current when its integration region coincides
with the full plasma cross-section.

Sign convention: Positive when the integrated conventional-current
contribution is along the selected positive component direction; for the
global toroidal current, this is increasing $\phi$, counterclockwise when
viewed from above along the positive vertical axis.

items.name: momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Vector Fick's-law transport coefficient relating the diffusive momentum flux
to the local momentum-density gradient, abstracting over plasma species,
neutral populations, charge states, and directional projections in a
magnetized plasma.
items.documentation:
Momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the
diffusive momentum flux and the negative local gradient of momentum density,
following a Fick's-law closure for the fluid momentum balance. Physically,
it encapsulates contributions from collisional viscosity, turbulent mixing,
charge-exchange friction, and diamagnetic drifts. As a vector quantity, its
radial, poloidal, toroidal, parallel, and vertical components capture the
strongly anisotropic transport characteristic of magnetized plasma, where
diffusivity along magnetic field lines greatly exceeds cross-field values.

The diffusive momentum flux density component along direction $\hat{e}_i$ is

$$
\Gamma_{m,i} = -D_{m,i} \frac{\partial (m n v_i)}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $D_{m,i}$ is the momentum diffusivity component, $m$ is particle mass,
$n$ is number density, and $v_i$ is the fluid velocity component along
$\hat{e}_i$, making $m n v_i$ the local momentum density.

This parent name abstracts over species-resolved and process-attributed
children including plasma_momentum_diffusivity for the total plasma and
analogous neutral-population variants; the
[radial_plasma_momentum_diffusion_coefficient](name:flux_surface_normal_plasma_momentum_diffusivity)
is the cross-field specialization and
[parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity](name:parallel_edge_plasma_momentum_diffusivity)
is the field-aligned form. Values are inferred from fluid transport
simulations by computing the diffusive momentum flux relative to the local
momentum-density gradient, or estimated analytically from neoclassical and
turbulence theory.

items.name: normalized_fluctuating_electron_density
items.description:
Normalized fluctuating electron density is the electron-density fluctuation
level given by the fluctuation amplitude divided by a reference electron
density. It represents the relative amplitude dn_e/n_e, not a signed
instantaneous perturbation.
items.documentation:
Normalized fluctuating electron density is the relative amplitude level of
fluctuations in [electron density](name:electron_density). It is formed from
the amplitude of the fluctuating component of electron density and the
reference electron density about which that fluctuation is defined.

The normalized fluctuation level is defined by

$$
\left(\frac{\delta n_e}{n_e}\right)_\mathrm{amp} = \frac{A[\tilde n_e]}{n_{e,\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $A[\tilde n_e]$ is the amplitude measure of the fluctuating component
of [electron density](name:electron_density), and $n_{e,\mathrm{ref}}$ is
the reference [electron density](name:electron_density) for the same plasma
region and fluctuation definition.

This is an amplitude-level quantity: $A[\tilde n_e]$ is non-negative and may
represent the explicitly defined rms, spectral, envelope, or other
fluctuation amplitude convention. It is distinct from the signed
instantaneous fractional perturbation $\tilde n_e/n_{e,\mathrm{ref}}$.

items.name: toroidal_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Toroidal component of the volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque on
thermal ions of a selected charge state, giving the net rate of toroidal
angular momentum transfer to that ion population by collisions.
items.documentation:
The toroidal projection of the volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional torque
vector
[thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions),
restricted to thermal ions of a selected ionic charge state $Z$. It is
defined as:

$$
\tau_\phi(Z) = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}(Z)
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}(Z)$ is the volume-integrated
Coulomb-collisional torque vector for ions in charge state $Z$, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector.

This scalar captures the net toroidal angular momentum deposited per unit
time into the specified thermal ion charge state by all Coulomb-collisional
partners, including fast particles, electrons, and background ion species.
It is volume-integrated over the plasma, not a local density; the
density-form analog for fast ions is
[toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions).
For the analogous thermal electron quantity see
[toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when the net collisional angular momentum transfer
to the ion charge state is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil
items.description:
Vertical Z coordinate of the Rogowski coil position in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measured along the machine symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
The vertical Z coordinate locates the Rogowski coil along the machine
symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$Z$ measures height above the $Z = 0$ reference plane. Together with the
major radius given by
[radial_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil](name:radial_coordinate_of_rogowski_coil),
it fully specifies the coil's position in a poloidal cross-section, which is
required to associate the enclosed-current measurement with the correct
plasma geometry and to provide geometric inputs for magnetic equilibrium
reconstruction.

This coordinate is a fixed geometric parameter established from engineering
metrology of the installed coil. The same vertical-coordinate convention is
applied to
[vertical_coordinate_of_flux_loop](name:vertical_coordinate_of_flux_loop)
and vertical_coordinate_of_coil_conductor across the magnetic diagnostics
family.

Sign convention: Positive when the coil is located above the $Z = 0$
reference plane, in the upward direction along the machine symmetry axis.

items.name: line_averaged_beryllium_density
items.description:
Chord-average of the beryllium ion number density along a diagnostic line of
sight, equal to the path integral of the local beryllium density divided by
the chord length.
items.documentation:
The line-averaged beryllium ion number density quantifies the mean beryllium
ion content along a plasma diagnostic chord, normalized by chord length. It
is the chord-integrated analog of the local
[beryllium_density](name:beryllium_density) and is the most directly
accessible measure of beryllium impurity concentration from line-of-sight
diagnostics.

The quantity is defined as:

$$
\bar{n}_{Be} = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_{Be}(l) \, dl
$$

where $n_{Be}(l)$ is the local beryllium ion number density at path
coordinate $l$ along the chord and $L$ is the total chord length.

Inferred from passive spectroscopy of beryllium emission lines by inverting
chord-integrated emission intensities using atomic emissivity coefficients;
the result aggregates contributions from all beryllium ionization states
present along the chord. The
[volume_averaged_beryllium_density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density)
provides a complementary global volume average, while
[beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis)
gives the local on-axis value.

Sign convention: Positive when beryllium ions populate the measurement
chord.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux is the signed magnetic flux through a horizontal disk
centered on the toroidal symmetry axis, labeling magnetic surfaces in
axisymmetric equilibrium.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux is the net magnetic flux through a horizontal disk
centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle
through the evaluation point. It specializes [magnetic
flux](name:magnetic_flux) by specifying the integration surface and its
orientation. In axisymmetric equilibrium, its level sets define magnetic
surfaces.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above,
and $Z$ is vertical height. The full poloidal magnetic flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}(R,Z) \equiv \psi(R,Z) = 2\pi \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}$, also denoted $\psi$, is the poloidal magnetic
flux, $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, and $R'$ is the radial
integration variable. The factor $2\pi$ accounts for integration around the
complete toroidal circle.

This quantity includes contributions from plasma currents and external
sources, unlike [external magnetic flux](name:external_magnetic_flux), which
excludes the plasma-generated contribution. It is the full flux, not flux
divided by $2\pi$, a normalized coordinate, or a cross-sectional average. It
differs from [toroidal magnetic flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux), which
integrates the toroidal magnetic field through a poloidal cross-section.

The [magnetic-axis value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis) and
[plasma-boundary value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary) are
evaluations of this same function and provide the endpoint references for
poloidal-flux normalization. For nested surfaces enclosing positive toroidal
plasma current flowing toward increasing $\phi$, the poloidal flux decreases
from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic field threading the horizontal
disk has a net component toward increasing $Z$, along the upward surface
normal.

items.name: neutral_species_particle_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating neutral-species particle
flux to neutral-species number-density gradients, with directional
components represented by more specific quantities.
items.documentation:
Neutral-species particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient
for particle spreading driven by a neutral-species number-density gradient.
It is the neutral-species specialization of [particle
diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), with directional components
represented by more specific quantities.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux of neutral
species $s$ is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{n},s,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\mathrm{n},s,i}\,\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{n},s}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{n},s,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle
flux of neutral species $s$ along direction $i$, $D_{\mathrm{n},s,i}$ is the
corresponding neutral-species particle diffusivity component,
$n_{\mathrm{n},s}$ is the number density of neutral species $s$, and $x_i$
is the coordinate along the resolved transport direction. The minus sign
defines down-gradient diffusive transport for a positive coefficient.

This quantity selects the neutral-species population but does not select a
transport direction, neutral state, or microscopic mechanism.
Direction-specific instances include [parallel neutral-species particle
diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_species_particle_diffusivity). When a
neutral species is decomposed into neutral states, the species-level
diffusivity is the density-weighted mean over those states; the
state-resolved counterpart is [neutral-state particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_state_particle_diffusivity).

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_control_surface
items.description:
Toroidal angle locating each point of a control surface about the machine
symmetry axis, measured in the right-handed cylindrical frame from the
facility-defined zero direction.
items.documentation:
The toroidal angle identifies the azimuthal location of a point on the
control surface about the machine symmetry axis. It is the geometrical
coordinate defined for [toroidal angle](name:toroidal_angle), with the
control-surface locus providing the points to which it applies.

For a point with Cartesian coordinates $x$ and $y$ in the right-handed
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, the angle in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame is defined by:

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(y,x) \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $R$ is the major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, and the zero of
$\phi$ follows the facility-defined reference direction. The angle is
periodic, so values differing by an integer multiple of $2\pi$ represent the
same toroidal direction; it is distinct from the vertical coordinate of the
control surface.

Sign convention: Positive when $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when
viewed from above the $+\hat{Z}$ direction.

items.name: volume_averaged_time_derivative_of_electron_density
items.description:
Rate of change of the electron number density averaged over the confined
plasma volume, with positive values indicating increasing mean density.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the temporal rate of change of the electron number density
after volume averaging over the confined plasma volume. Positive values
indicate increasing mean electron density, while negative values indicate
decreasing mean electron density.

For a fixed averaging volume, the defining relation is

$$
\frac{d\langle n_e\rangle_V}{dt} = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \frac{\partial n_e}{\partial t}\,dV
$$

where $n_e$ is the local electron number density, $V$ is the confined plasma
volume, and $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).

The volume-average operation is applied to the electron density before time
differentiation. This distinguishes the quantity from the more general [time
derivative of electron density](name:time_derivative_of_electron_density),
which does not specify volume averaging.

items.name: carbon_density
items.description:
Carbon density is the local number density of elemental carbon in the
plasma, summed over neutral carbon atoms and all ionic charge states through
fully stripped C6+.
items.documentation:
Carbon density is the local number density of elemental carbon in the
plasma, summed over neutral carbon atoms and all ionic charge states through
fully stripped $C^{6+}$. It represents the elemental carbon population per
physical volume, independent of ionization balance.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by the number-density sum:

$$
n_C = \sum_{z=0}^{6} n_{C^{z+}}
$$

where $n_C$ is the carbon density, $z=0$ denotes neutral carbon,
$z=1,\ldots,6$ denote ionic charge states, and $n_{C^{z+}}$ is the number
density of carbon in charge state $z$.

This quantity is unweighted by charge, mass, or radiation emissivity and is
distinct from electron density, charge density, and individual charge-state
densities. Spatially averaged or locus-specific carbon-density quantities
include
[volume_averaged_carbon_density](name:volume_averaged_carbon_density),
flux_surface_averaged_carbon_density_at_plasma_boundary, and the ion-only
divertor-target quantity
[carbon_density_at_divertor_target](name:carbon_density_at_divertor_target).

items.name: radial_momentum_flux
items.description:
Rate of transport of radial linear momentum per unit area across an oriented
surface in the plasma, combining convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous
or turbulent-stress contributions, with radial defined along increasing
major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial momentum flux is the radial component of the linear-momentum flux
crossing an oriented surface in the plasma. It includes convective transport
together with isotropic pressure and viscous or turbulent stress
contributions projected onto the $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from
the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The radial projection of the momentum current through an oriented surface
is:

$$
\Gamma_{\Pi,R} = \hat{R}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\Pi,R}$ is this radial momentum flux, $\hat{R}$ is the radial
basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}$ is the tensor associated with [momentum
flux](name:momentum_flux), and $\hat{n}$ is the chosen unit normal of the
oriented surface. For a single plasma fluid, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}$ contains the
convective term $\rho\mathbf{v}\mathbf{v}$, scalar-pressure term
$p\mathbf{I}$, and viscous or turbulent stress term $\boldsymbol{\pi}$,
where $\rho$ is mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ is bulk flow velocity, $p$ is
scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ is the identity tensor, and $\boldsymbol{\pi}$
is the viscous or turbulent stress tensor.

This name denotes the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ radial
projection of the momentum current, not a flux-surface-normal projection and
not a derivative with respect to a radial flux label. It is the radial
direction-resolved form of [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux), distinct
from other direction-resolved or population-resolved momentum-flux
quantities.

Sign convention: Positive when the momentum current through the oriented
surface has a component in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Parallel current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed projection
of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic-drift current-density
contribution onto the local magnetic-field direction.
items.documentation:
Parallel current density due to diamagnetic drift is the signed
field-aligned scalar projection of the pressure-gradient-driven current
described by [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It represents the
component along the local magnetic-field line, including field-aligned
return-current contributions associated with maintaining current continuity.

The field-aligned projection is defined by

$$
j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [diamagnetic-drift current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the
local magnetic field.

This quantity is the generic parallel component of the diamagnetic-drift
current-density contribution. The [Pfirsch-Schlüter diamagnetic-drift
current
density](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is
a specific field-aligned return-current contribution, and [parallel
Pfirsch-Schlüter diamagnetic-drift current
density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
denotes that contribution when represented explicitly as a parallel
projection. It is distinct from [toroidal current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which is
projected onto $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic-drift current-density
contribution has a component in the direction of the local magnetic-field
unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: argon_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of argon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over positive ionization
states and excluding neutral argon.
items.documentation:
Number density of argon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the argon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The charge-state-summed argon number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the total argon-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the local number density of argon ions with
positive charge state $q$, and $q$ is the integer argon charge-state index.

This quantity applies to the argon-ion population immediately upstream of
the electrostatic sheath at a divertor target and is summed over all
positive argon charge states from singly ionized through fully stripped
argon. Neutral argon atoms and other neutral argon forms are excluded, as
are electrons and ions of other elements.

This is a local species density rather than a density integrated over the
target surface or summed over all plasma species. The corresponding argon
quantity at a limiter, [argon density at the
limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter), has the same charge-state
aggregation but a different evaluation locus; unlike [electron density at
the divertor target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target), this
quantity describes argon ions rather than free electrons.

items.name: volume_averaged_krypton_density
items.description:
Number density of krypton, volume-averaged over the plasma, summed over
neutral krypton and all ionized charge states through fully stripped Kr36+.
items.documentation:
Number density of krypton, volume-averaged over the plasma, summed over
neutral krypton and all ionized charge states through fully stripped
Kr$^{36+}$.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} \left(\sum_{q=0}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}}^{(q)}(\mathbf{r})\right) d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and
$n_{\mathrm{Kr}}^{(q)}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local number density of krypton
in charge state $q$; $q=0$ denotes neutral krypton and $q=36$ denotes fully
stripped krypton.

Unlike the local [krypton density](name:krypton_density), this quantity
includes neutral krypton and applies a plasma-volume average. It is an
absolute elemental density, distinct from the normalized abundance in the
[volume-averaged krypton-to-electron density
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_krypton_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density).

items.name: toroidal_total_momentum_flux
items.description:
Toroidal total momentum flux is the stress-like rate per unit area at which
the toroidal component of plasma linear momentum is transported across an
oriented surface. Contributions from included plasma species and charge
states are combined; for flux-surface transport, it is the outward
flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Toroidal total momentum flux is the stress-like flux density of the toroidal
component of plasma [momentum](name:momentum) across an oriented surface. It
combines contributions from included plasma species, with charge-state
contributions summed over all charge states. It describes transported linear
momentum, not stored momentum or a momentum source or torque.

The toroidal momentum flux through an oriented surface is the projection of
the total momentum-flux tensor onto the toroidal direction and the surface
normal:

$$
\Gamma_{\phi n}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \cdot \left(\sum_s \boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{tot}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

Here, $\Gamma_{\phi n}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is this flux, $s$ indexes the
included plasma species and charge states, and
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total momentum-flux tensor
contributed by $s$, including convective, isotropic-pressure, and viscous or
turbulent-stress contributions as applicable. The vector
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the oriented surface normal. The toroidal
direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The quantity is defined locally across an oriented surface. For transport
across magnetic flux surfaces, the crossing direction is the outward
flux-surface normal and the flux is the flux-surface average; this
surface-normal direction is distinct from the toroidal momentum direction.
The quantity is the toroidal component of [total momentum
flux](name:total_momentum_flux), rather than a flux in the toroidal
direction.

Sign convention: Positive when positive toroidal linear momentum, directed
toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, is transported outward across the
flux surface.

items.name: temperature_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description:
Thermodynamic temperature of the soft X-ray detector assembly, describing
its physical thermal state for calibration and monitoring rather than a
plasma temperature inferred from radiation.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the thermodynamic temperature of the physical soft X-ray
detector assembly and describes the thermal state of its hardware.

It applies to the detector object as a whole, with no implied plasma
population, spatial subcomponent, or charge-state aggregation. It is
distinct from the plasma electron temperature inferred from detected soft
X-ray radiation and does not represent a photon-energy or spectral-response
quantity.

The temperature is the thermal operating state relevant to calibration and
hardware-condition monitoring. It is conceptually analogous to [temperature
of neutron detector](name:temperature_of_neutron_detector), while [spectral
efficiency of soft X-ray
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_soft_xray_detector) describes
photon-registration probability rather than detector hardware temperature.

items.name: iron_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the iron ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local iron-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all iron ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the iron ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local iron-ion count per physical volume at that location. It
represents iron ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral iron, or
another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Fe,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Fe,axis}}$ is the iron-ion number density at the magnetic
axis, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of iron ions summed over all iron
ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete ionic iron population at that location,
with all iron charge states aggregated, and is neither a flux-surface or
volume integral nor a neutral-iron density.

This is the iron-specific realization of the population-independent [density
at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It is distinguished
from [hydrogen density at the magnetic
axis](name:hydrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts hydrogen ions,
and from [iron density at the internal transport
barrier](name:iron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), which is
evaluated on the flux surface assigned to that barrier rather than at the
magnetic axis.

items.name: xenon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of xenon ions at the internal transport barrier, the
flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport
permits steep radial impurity-density gradients to form; summed over all
xenon ion charge states and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of xenon ions at the internal transport barrier is
the local xenon-ion particle density, summed over all xenon ion charge
states, on the flux surface selected as the barrier reference location. The
internal transport barrier is a confined-plasma flux-surface region where
locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep radial
impurity-density gradients to form. Xenon (atomic number $Z = 54$) is a
high-$Z$ noble-gas impurity species.

The charge-state-summed xenon-ion density at the barrier reference surface
is the sum of zeroth velocity moments of the xenon ion distribution
functions:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_{q=1}^{54} \int f_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v}, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\, d^3v
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the elemental xenon ion number density, $q$ is
the xenon ion charge number, $f_{\mathrm{Xe}^{q+}}$ is the distribution
function of xenon ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, and $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the scalar flux-surface label
identifying the internal-transport-barrier reference surface. The range
$q=1,\ldots,54$ spans all positive xenon ion charge states and excludes
neutral xenon atoms.

At the species level this per-volume particle amount is charge-state-summed:
charge-state-resolved xenon ion densities are distinct populations, and
summing them over all positive charge states recovers this elemental
density. It is the xenon-specific instance of
[density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and the barrier-local counterpart of [xenon_density](name:xenon_density),
distinct from
[electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and from other noble-gas impurity densities at the same locus.

items.name: electron_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Number density of electrons at the H-mode pedestal top, giving the
electron-density pedestal height as a local particle concentration.
items.documentation:
Number density of electron

The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the electron
distribution:

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt}) = \int f_e(\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt}$ is the
position at the pedestal top, $f_e$ is the electron number distribution in
position and velocity space, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, and $d^3v$
is the velocity-space volume element.

All free electrons contribute; ions and bound electrons are excluded. This
is a local density, neither flux-surface averaged nor line-of-sight
averaged. Pedestal height here denotes a density level, not a spatial width
or a density gradient.

It is the electron-specific member of [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), not a sum over different plasma species.
[Electron density at the pedestal
maximum](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum) describes the same
electron population evaluated at a different locus.

items.name: ratio_of_vertical_vorticity_to_major_radius
items.description:
Vertical plasma vorticity divided by the local major radius, retaining the
signed rotation rate about the vertical axis with inverse-length scaling.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the major-radius-scaled form of [vertical
vorticity](name:vertical_vorticity), measuring local bulk-plasma rotation
about the vertical direction per unit major radius. It is defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\omega_Z^*(R,\phi,Z)=\frac{\omega_Z(R,\phi,Z)}{R},\qquad \omega_Z=(\nabla\times\mathbf{v})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
bulk-velocity vector, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient, and
$\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The scaling applies to the
vertical-vorticity component itself and does not represent the full
[vorticity](name:vorticity) vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the bulk-flow rotation is in the $+Z$ sense,
namely counterclockwise in the $(R,\phi)$ plane when viewed from $+Z$.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_closest_wall_point
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate R of the first-wall point nearest the plasma
boundary, measured from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the major-radius coordinate of the wall point selected as
closest to the plasma boundary. It identifies that point’s perpendicular
distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, phi, Z)$ frame.

The defining geometric relation is

$$
R_{\mathrm{cw}} = \left\lVert \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{cw},\perp} \right\rVert
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{cw}}$ is the radial coordinate of the closest wall point
and $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{cw},\perp}$ is the perpendicular displacement
vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to that point.

The scope is the single wall point selected by its minimum proximity to the
plasma boundary. This is a pointwise geometric coordinate with no
plasma-population dependence and no averaging, summation, or integration. It
is not the wall-to-boundary separation distance, nor is “closest” a
statement that the point has the smallest major radius among all wall
points.

This quantity is a locus-specific instance of [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), restricted to the closest wall point
rather than an arbitrary geometric reference position.

items.name: average_external_magnetic_flux
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux generated by external circuits and averaged over the
plasma cross-section, with weighting defined by each concrete variant.
items.documentation:
External magnetic flux averaged over the plasma poloidal cross-section
represents the externally generated contribution to the poloidal flux
function, excluding flux produced by the plasma current. It is an
averaging-level specialization of external magnetic flux; concrete variants
can differ in their weighting and normalization.

For a weighting function $w(\mathbf{x})$, the general weighted average is

$$
\langle \psi_{\rm ext} \rangle_w = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{P}} w(\mathbf{x})\,\psi_{\rm ext}(\mathbf{x})\,dS}{\int_{\mathcal{P}} w(\mathbf{x})\,dS}
$$

where $\psi_{\rm ext}(\mathbf{x})$ is the externally generated poloidal
magnetic flux, $\mathbf{x}$ is position in the plasma poloidal cross-section
$\mathcal{P}$, $w(\mathbf{x})$ is the prescribed averaging weight, and $dS$
is the cross-sectional area element. The representative [current-weighted
average external magnetic
flux](name:current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux) uses the
toroidal current density as $w$ and the plasma current as the normalization.

Sign convention: Positive when the underlying poloidal flux is positive for
a vertical magnetic field in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis on the defining horizontal
disk.

items.name: parallel_vorticity
items.description:
Projection of the curl of plasma center-of-mass velocity along the local
magnetic field, measuring signed local rotation of the bulk flow about that
direction.
items.documentation:
Parallel vorticity is the component of plasma [vorticity](name:vorticity)
along the local magnetic-field direction. For solid-body rotation, it is
twice the component of a fluid element's angular velocity along that
direction.

The field-aligned projection of the bulk-velocity curl is defined by:

$$
\omega_{\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf{b}}\cdot\boldsymbol{\omega} = \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}\cdot(\nabla\times\mathbf{v})
$$

where $\omega_{\parallel}$ is parallel vorticity, $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is
the full plasma vorticity vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field,
$|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is its direction unit
vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity), and $\nabla\times$ is the curl
operator with right-handed orientation.

The scope is the local single-fluid plasma bulk flow wherever the magnetic
field is nonzero. Constituent flows enter through the mass-weighted
center-of-mass velocity; this is not a species- or charge-state-resolved
vorticity. No surface, volume, or time averaging is implied. It is not
vorticity magnitude, flow shear, strain rate, velocity divergence, or
magnetic-field-line twist.

The projection is applied after taking the curl of the full velocity field;
[parallel plasma velocity](name:parallel_plasma_velocity) alone does not
determine it. Unlike [toroidal vorticity](name:toroidal_vorticity), which
projects onto the geometric toroidal direction, parallel vorticity follows
the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the bulk-flow curl has a component along the
local magnetic field, corresponding to rotation in the right-handed sense
about that direction.

items.name: oxygen_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Oxygen density at a limiter is the local number density of oxygen ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface,
summed over all oxygen ionization states from O+ through O8+ and excluding
neutral oxygen atoms.
items.documentation:
Oxygen density at a limiter is the local number density of oxygen ions in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or
sheath entrance at the limiter. It is summed over all oxygen ionization
states from O$^+$ through O$^{8+}$, and excludes neutral oxygen atoms.

For oxygen ion charge states from singly ionized to fully stripped, the
charge-state-summed limiter density is defined as:

$$
n_{\mathrm{O},\mathrm{lim}} = \sum_{q=1}^{8} n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+},\mathrm{lim}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O},\mathrm{lim}}$ is the oxygen ion density at the
limiter, $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+},\mathrm{lim}}$ is the local density of oxygen
ions with charge state $q$, and the upper limit is the nuclear charge of
oxygen.

This quantity is species-specific and charge-state-summed; it is not the
neutral oxygen density,
[electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter), or
[total_ion_density_at_limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter). At the
sheath entrance, oxygen charge-state densities contribute to quasineutrality
through their charge-weighted sum and to the local effective charge. The
analogous oxygen density at divertor target surfaces is
[oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target).

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of the nitrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for nitrogen ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Number density of the nitrogen species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for nitrogen ions at the sheath entrance
immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the
nitrogen-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local nitrogen-ion number density is defined by the differential
particle count:

$$
n_N = \frac{dN_N}{dV}
$$

where $N_N$ is the number of nitrogen ions in a small plasma volume $V$
whose center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side at the
divertor target.

This quantity applies to the nitrogen-ion population immediately adjacent to
the divertor target and is summed over all positive nitrogen ionization
states. The aggregation counts each nitrogen ion once, regardless of its
charge state.

Neutral nitrogen atoms are excluded, as are nitrogen-bearing particles that
are not represented as nitrogen ions. This quantity is distinct from
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target),
which counts free electrons, and from
[neon_density_at_divertor_target](name:neon_density_at_divertor_target),
which applies the same target-local density definition to neon ions.

As a species-specific component, this quantity is one member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target); the parent
represents the same target-local number-density concept for a specified
species or species group.

items.name: torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description:
Torque density due to j cross b force is the vector density of
angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force acting on a
specified plasma population. It is the parent concept for
orbit-class-restricted and directionally projected forms.
items.documentation:
Torque density due to $j \times B$ force is the local vector density of
angular-momentum transfer produced by the Lorentz force density acting on a
specified plasma population. It represents the electromagnetic torque
density before any optional orbit-class selection, flux-surface averaging,
or directional projection is applied.

The local torque density is defined as the moment of the Lorentz force
density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{r}(\mathbf{x}) \times \left[\mathbf{j}(\mathbf{x}) \times \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})\right]
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from the chosen torque reference
point to position $\mathbf{x}$, $\mathbf{j}$ is the electric current density
associated with the force acting on the population, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the
magnetic field.

This parent quantity denotes the shared torque-density concept. Specialized
names may restrict the orbit class, such as
[co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force](name:co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force)
or
[trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force](name:trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force),
or may take a directional projection such as
[toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).
A toroidal projection is onto $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{J\times B}$ points in the positive direction of its
stated basis vector; for a toroidal projection this is $+\hat{\phi}$, the
direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

items.name: tungsten_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of tungsten ions evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over all tungsten ion
charge states and excluding neutral tungsten.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of tungsten ions evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the
tungsten-ion population at that flux-surface location.

The number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{W}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N_{\mathrm{W}}}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the tungsten-ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{W}}$
is the number of counted tungsten ions, and $V$ is volume.

This quantity is the tungsten-specific member of [density at the internal
transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier). The count is
summed over all tungsten ionic charge states and excludes neutral tungsten.
It is evaluated at the internal transport barrier rather than at a divertor
target, as distinguished by [tungsten density at the divertor
target](name:tungsten_density_at_divertor_target).

items.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Toroidal beryllium-ion bulk velocity at the magnetic axis, density-weighted
over all beryllium ionization states in the right-handed (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal beryllium-ion bulk-flow velocity is the charge-state-aggregated
toroidal component of beryllium ion motion evaluated at the magnetic axis.
Neutral beryllium is excluded.

$$
V_{phi,\mathrm{Be}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}} V_{phi,\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

Here $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the density of beryllium ions
in charge state $z$ at the magnetic axis, and
$V_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}^{\mathrm{axis}}$ is that charge state's toroidal
bulk-flow component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The
denominator is the [beryllium ion density at the magnetic
axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis), and the sum covers all
beryllium ionic charge states.

Sign convention: Positive when the beryllium-ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless toroidal ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient
that scales the free-streaming bound on toroidal momentum transport for a
specified ion charge state.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion charge-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter parameter for momentum transport of a specified ion charge
state in the geometric toroidal direction. It is the toroidal component of
the vector quantity [ion charge-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

If $\Pi_{\phi}$ is the modeled toroidal momentum flux and
$\Pi_{\phi,\mathrm{fs}}$ is its collisionless free-streaming reference
bound, the limiter constrains their magnitudes according to

$$
|\Pi_{\phi}| \leq \alpha_{\phi}|\Pi_{\phi,\mathrm{fs}}|
$$

where $\alpha_{\phi}$ is this coefficient and the toroidal direction is the
direction of increasing $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame. The coefficient limits the magnitude of the modeled flux; it does not
define the flux direction or its sign. The corresponding axis-specific
quantity for poloidal transport is the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum
flux-limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).

items.name: plasma_magnetic_field
items.description:
Plasma magnetic-field strength of the local magnetic induction associated
with the confined plasma, including equilibrium and plasma-interior
perturbed contributions while excluding the separate vacuum-field
definition.
items.documentation:
The plasma magnetic field $B_{\rm plasma}$ is the scalar magnitude of the
local [magnetic induction](name:magnetic_field) associated with the confined
plasma. It represents field strength at a plasma location, including
equilibrium and plasma-interior perturbed contributions when present, rather
than retaining vector direction or selecting a signed component.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, its value may be written
from the components of the associated plasma magnetic-induction vector as

$$
B_{\rm plasma}=\left|\mathbf{B}_{\rm plasma}\right|=\sqrt{B_{R,{\rm plasma}}^2+B_{\phi,{\rm plasma}}^2+B_{Z,{\rm plasma}}^2}
$$

where $B_{\rm plasma}$ is the plasma magnetic-field strength,
$\mathbf{B}_{\rm plasma}$ is the local plasma magnetic-induction vector,
$B_{R,{\rm plasma}}$ is its signed component along increasing major radius
$R$, $B_{\phi,{\rm plasma}}$ is its signed component along increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$, and $B_{Z,{\rm plasma}}$ is its signed component
along increasing vertical height $Z$.

This quantity applies locally within the confined plasma region and has no
species population. Its aggregation convention is a point value of
magnetic-field strength, not a spatial average, flux-surface average, volume
integral, or finite-volume reduction.

This scalar magnitude is distinct from the vector [magnetic
induction](name:magnetic_field) and from component-resolved fields such as
the [toroidal magnetic field](name:toroidal_magnetic_field), [radial
magnetic field](name:radial_magnetic_field), and [vertical magnetic
field](name:vertical_magnetic_field), which retain directional sign. It is
also distinct from the [vacuum magnetic field](name:vacuum_magnetic_field),
which excludes plasma-current and plasma-interior contributions, and from
the [perturbed plasma magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field),
which denotes the perturbation contribution rather than the total local
plasma-associated field strength.

items.name: electron_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Electron number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a
plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance.
items.documentation:
Electron density at a limiter is the local number density of electrons in
the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface.
The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or
sheath entrance.

$$
n_e(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_e}{dV}
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_e$ is the number
of electrons, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the limiter-side
evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Unlike ion density at a limiter, this quantity counts electrons only and
includes neither ions nor neutral atoms. It is the electron-specific member
of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and is distinct from
[electron density at the plasma
boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which uses a different
evaluation locus.

items.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective transport velocity relating the convective flux of major-radius
momentum to its density for one neutral species in a specified internal
quantum or energy state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective convection coefficient for transport of the
major-radius component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by one neutral
species in a specified internal quantum or energy state. Major-radius
momentum is the projection onto the direction of increasing $R$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The density-proportional convective contribution to the momentum flux is
defined by:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{conv}}_{0a,R;n} = V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{0a,R}\,g_{0a,R}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{conv}}_{0a,R;n}$ is the convective flux of major-radius
momentum through a surface with chosen unit normal $\hat{n}$,
$V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{0a,R}$ is this convection coefficient, and $g_{0a,R}$ is
the corresponding momentum density. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral
particles, $a$ identifies their internal state, and $n$ labels the
surface-normal flux direction. The momentum density is $g_{0a,R}=m_0
n_{0a}u_{0a,R}$, where $m_0$ is the neutral-particle mass, $n_{0a}$ is the
state-resolved number density, and $u_{0a,R}$ is the major-radius component
of the state-resolved mean translational velocity.

The major-radius label identifies the transported momentum component, not
the direction through which it is transported. The surface normal need not
coincide with the major-radius direction or a magnetic-flux-surface normal.
The coefficient excludes diffusive momentum transport and momentum source
terms. Unlike the [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), it is a
transport-closure coefficient and need not equal the particle-flow velocity.

This quantity applies to one neutral species and one internal state, without
summation over species or internal states. State-resolved convective fluxes
sum to the species-level convective flux associated with the [radial
neutral-species momentum convection
velocity](name:radial_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity); the
coefficients themselves are not summed.

Sign convention: Positive when the convective flux of major-radius momentum
along the chosen surface normal has the same sign as the corresponding
momentum density.

items.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description:
Rate of nuclear energy deposited throughout one breeder blanket module by
neutron interactions and associated photon absorption, excluding incident
and externally applied heat.
items.documentation:
Nuclear heating power of a breeder blanket module is the rate of nuclear
energy deposited within the material volume of one module by neutron
interactions and the absorption of primary or secondary photons. It is an
integrated deposition quantity, not incident radiation power or local power
density.

The module-integrated power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc,module}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{module}}} q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{nuc,module}}$ is the integrated nuclear heating power,
$V_{\mathrm{module}}$ is the module material volume,
$q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local nuclear heating power density in
W m$^{-3}$, $\mathbf{r}$ is position in the module in m, and $\mathrm{d}V$
is differential material volume in m$^{3}$.

The integration includes energy deposited in module materials by neutron and
photon interactions. It excludes unde posited incident radiation,
plasma-facing surface heat loads, and heat subsequently transferred to
coolant. It is distinct from the local nuclear power density of a breeder
blanket module, the layer-resolved [nuclear heating power of a breeder
blanket layer](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_layer), and the
blanket-wide [nuclear heating
power](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket).

items.name: thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket
items.description:
Thermal power of the breeder blanket is the integrated non-nuclear heat load
entering the blanket through its plasma-facing surface, excluding volumetric
neutron and photon heating. It is a blanket-level surface-deposition power,
distinct from module-level coolant heat removal.
items.documentation:
Thermal power of the breeder blanket is the total rate at which non-nuclear
thermal energy enters the breeder blanket through its plasma-facing surface.
It represents an integrated surface heat load on the blanket, not a local
heat-flux density.

For a surface heat-load representation, the integrated power is defined by
the area integral of the local non-nuclear heat flux entering the blanket:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,bb}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf,bb}}} q_{\mathrm{th}} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th,bb}}$ is the thermal power of the breeder blanket,
$A_{\mathrm{pf,bb}}$ is the plasma-facing surface area of the breeder
blanket included in the blanket-level total, $q_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local
non-nuclear heat-flux density directed into the blanket, and $dA$ is the
surface element.

This quantity excludes volumetric neutron and photon energy deposition in
blanket material, which is represented by
[nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket).
It also differs from thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module, which denotes
module-level thermal power associated with an individual breeder-blanket
module rather than the blanket-level plasma-facing surface load.

items.name: radius_of_passive_loop
items.description:
Radius of the annular cross-section of a passive conducting loop element is
the Euclidean distance from the cross-section center to a specified
conducting boundary. It is nonnegative and does not denote the loop center's
major-radius position.
items.documentation:
Radius of the annular cross-section of a passive conducting loop element is
the Euclidean distance, in the $(R,Z)$ plane at fixed toroidal angle $phi$
of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, phi, Z)$ frame, from the center of the
annular conductor cross-section to a specified conducting boundary of that
annulus. Here $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The boundary radius is defined by the poloidal-plane distance from the
cross-section center to the selected boundary point:

$$
r = \sqrt{(R_b - R_c)^2 + (Z_b - Z_c)^2}
$$

where $(R_c,Z_c)$ is the center position of the annular cross-section and
$(R_b,Z_b)$ is the selected boundary position in the same fixed-$phi$
plane; all coordinate components in the equation are expressed in meters.

This parent quantity abstracts over
[inner_radius_of_passive_loop](name:inner_radius_of_passive_loop) and
[outer_radius_of_passive_loop](name:outer_radius_of_passive_loop). It
satisfies $r \ge 0$ and is a size of the conductor cross-section, not a
signed component along $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ and not the
major-radius coordinate of the loop center. For a circular annulus,
[area_of_passive_loop](name:area_of_passive_loop) is related by
$A=\pi(r_\mathrm{outer}^2-r_\mathrm{inner}^2)$, and
thickness_of_passive_loop is $r_\mathrm{outer}-r_\mathrm{inner}$.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_effective_charge_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Flux-surface average of the ion-mixture effective charge over the entire
plasma-boundary surface, distinct from the local boundary value.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface average of the ion-mixture effective
charge over the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed flux
surface. It summarizes the charge composition across the complete boundary
surface rather than at a single location.

$$
\left\langle Z_{\mathrm{eff}} \right\rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi_b} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}\,d\ell/B_p}{\oint_{\psi_b} d\ell/B_p}, \qquad Z_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{\sum_i n_i Z_i^2}{n_e}
$$

Here $\psi_b$ labels the plasma-boundary flux surface, $d\ell$ is poloidal
arc length, $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, $n_i$ and $Z_i$
are the number density and charge number of ion population $i$, and $n_e$ is
the electron number density. The linked effective charge at the plasma
boundary denotes the corresponding local boundary quantity; this entry
denotes its flux-surface average.

items.name: accumulated_ethane_count
items.description:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of ethane molecules injected after
plasma breakdown, assigning 18 equivalent-electron counts to each neutral
C2H6 molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the post-breakdown cumulative ethane-gas inventory
expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral C2H6 molecule
contributes 18 counts: 12 from its two carbon atoms and 6 from its six
hydrogen atoms.

The accumulated count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 18\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the ethane molecule injection rate,
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation
time.

This quantity is the accumulated post-breakdown form of the ethane count
convention. It excludes ethane introduced during prefill, represented by
[ethane prefill count](name:ethane_prefill_count), and differs from the
instantaneous [ethane source rate](name:ethane_source_rate).

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_launching_position
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the beam launching position, measured from the
toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of launching position

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the coordinate is
defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate at the launching position, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantities $x$ and $y$
are the horizontal coordinates of the same position in a right-handed
Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, whose vertical $z$ axis coincides with the
toroidal symmetry axis.

This is a locus-specific specialization of
[radial_coordinate](name:radial_coordinate): it applies pointwise to the
specified beam launching position, rather than representing an average over
beams or coordinates along a beam trajectory. It is distinct from the
[radial coordinate of an electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:radial_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), which
locates the mirror's reference geometry rather than the beam launching
position.

items.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_halo_boundary
items.description:
Signed toroidal magnetic flux through the poloidal cross-section bounded by
the outermost flux surface of the halo-current region during a disruption.
items.documentation:
The toroidal magnetic flux function evaluated on the outermost flux surface
bounding the halo-current region during a disruption is the net toroidal
magnetic-field flux through the enclosed poloidal cross-section. It is
distinct from the [toroidal halo current](name:toroidal_halo_current), which
describes current rather than magnetic flux.

The flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathcal{A}_h)=\int_{\mathcal{A}_h}\mathbf{B}\cdot\hat{\phi}\,dA=\int_{\mathcal{A}_h}B_{\phi}\,dA
$$

where $\mathcal{A}_h$ is the poloidal area enclosed by the halo boundary,
$\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field in tesla, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal
unit vector, $B_{\phi}$ is its toroidal component, and $dA$ is the poloidal
area element. The boundary value is the halo-region counterpart of [toroidal
magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal magnetic field points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: electron_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the electron population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local electron count per physical volume at that location.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the electron population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local electron count per physical volume at that location. It
represents electrons specifically, rather than ions, neutrals, or another
plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{e,\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_e}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{e,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the electron number density at the magnetic
axis, $N_e$ is the number of electrons, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete electron population at that location
and is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor an ion or neutral
density.

This is the electron-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It must be
distinguished from [total ion density at the magnetic
axis](name:total_ion_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts ions, and from
[electron temperature at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis), which characterizes
electron energy rather than particle count.

items.name: velocity_due_to_convection
items.description:
A vector velocity representing non-diffusive convective transport of plasma
energy, internal state, or momentum.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective vector velocity associated with convective,
or advective, transport of a plasma quantity. It describes the motion of the
transported quantity rather than diffusive spreading or the transported flux
itself.

For a transported density $Q$, the convective flux is defined by

$$
\mathbf{F}^{\mathrm{conv}}_Q = Q\,\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\mathbf{F}^{\mathrm{conv}}_Q$ is the convective flux, $Q$ is the
local density of the transported quantity, and $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{conv}}$
is this velocity. For vector or tensor quantities, the product is
interpreted componentwise or as the corresponding dyadic flux.

The same parent quantity is specialized by the transported channel in
[energy velocity due to convection](name:energy_velocity_due_to_convection),
internal-state velocity due to convection, and momentum velocity due to
convection. It excludes diffusive transport contributions.

Sign convention: Positive when a vector component points along the
corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: power_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description:
Band-integrated radiant power received by a soft X-ray detector channel over
its selected photon-energy band or bands.
items.documentation:
Soft X-ray detector power is the radiant power carried by incident soft
X-ray photons and received by one detector channel after spectral selection.
It represents radiation power rather than the detector’s electrical output.

For a selected photon-energy band, the received power is defined by:

$$
P_{\mathcal{B}} = \int_{\mathcal{B}} E\,\Phi_E(E)\,dE
$$

where $P_{\mathcal{B}}$ is the received power for band $\mathcal{B}$, $E$ is
photon energy, $\Phi_E(E)$ is the photon arrival-rate density as a function
of photon energy, $\mathcal{B}$ is the selected energy interval, and $dE$ is
an infinitesimal photon-energy interval.

The quantity applies to soft X-ray radiation received by a particular
detector channel and is integrated over photon energy within its selected
bandpass. It is not summed over detector channels, viewing directions, or
distinct energy bands; when multiple bands are resolved, each band has its
own band-integrated received-power value. It excludes plasma-emitted power
before arrival at the detector and electrical power generated by detector
electronics.

The quantity is distinct from
[spectral_efficiency_of_soft_xray_detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_soft_xray_detector),
which describes the probability of registering an incident photon rather
than the received radiant power. It is also distinct from
[hard_xray_brightness](name:hard_xray_brightness), which describes photon
radiance rather than the power collected by a channel over its energy band
and collection geometry.

items.name: thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total
thermal-ion population from a fast-particle distribution, summed over all
thermal ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the
complete thermal-ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with a
colliding fast-particle distribution. It aggregates all thermal ion species
and charge states without resolving the receiving ion species or charge
state.

The volume-integrated thermal-ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm th\,ion,coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm th\,ion,coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm th\,ion,coll}$ is the local collisional power density
transferred into the aggregate thermal-ion population and $V$ is the plasma
volume. The quantity is the thermal-ion counterpart of [fast ion power due
to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions) and is a
population-resolved component of [ion power due to
collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions). Charge-state-resolved
components include [thermal ion charge-state power due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net
energy into the complete thermal-ion population.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_dr_dz_zero_point
items.description:
Radial coordinate of the dR/dZ zero point is the R coordinate, in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of a plasma-boundary or separatrix
point where R is locally stationary with respect to Z.
items.documentation:
Radial coordinate of the dR/dZ zero point is the $R$ coordinate, in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of a specified point on a
plasma-boundary or separatrix contour where $R$ is locally stationary with
respect to $Z$. In this frame, $R$ is major radius measured from the
toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

The coordinate is defined by the stationary-radius condition on the
specified contour:

$$
R_{\mathrm{dR/dZ=0}} = R(P_0), \qquad \left.\frac{dR}{dZ}\right|_{C,P_0} = 0
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{dR/dZ=0}}$ is the radial coordinate of the dR/dZ zero
point, $P_0$ is the specified dR/dZ zero point, $C$ is the plasma-boundary
or separatrix contour on which $P_0$ lies, $R(P_0)$ is the major-radius
coordinate of $P_0$, $Z$ is the vertical-height coordinate, and $dR/dZ$ is
the derivative of the contour coordinate $R$ with respect to $Z$ along $C$.

The scope is a single specified geometric point on the contour; the value is
not an average over the contour, over toroidal angle $\phi$, or over all
stationary points. If several points on the contour satisfy $dR/dZ=0$, the
definition does not by itself impose an inboard, outboard, upper, or lower
selection rule; each specified zero point has its own radial-coordinate
value.

This quantity is only the cylindrical $R$ coordinate of the point, not a
flux-surface-normal displacement or a flux-label coordinate. Together with
the vertical coordinate of the dR/dZ zero point, it locates the point in the
poloidal $(R, Z)$ cross-section at fixed $\phi$ of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is distinct from the [radial coordinate
of an X-point](name:radial_coordinate_of_x_point), which locates a magnetic
null on a separatrix rather than a radial extremum of a boundary or
separatrix contour.

items.name: ion_average_temperature_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion
population at the magnetic axis, with all ion species and charge states
contributing according to their number densities. The magnetic axis is the
geometric center of the nested closed magnetic flux surfaces, where the
poloidal magnetic flux is stationary.
items.documentation:
Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion
population at the magnetic axis is the local ion temperature obtained by
weighting each thermal ion species and charge state by its local number
density. The magnetic axis is the geometric center of the nested closed
magnetic flux surfaces, equivalently the locus where the poloidal magnetic
flux is stationary.

For resolved ion populations, the effective temperature is defined by the
density-weighted average at the magnetic axis:

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}}^{\mathrm{axis}} = \frac{\sum_s \sum_\zeta n_{s,\zeta}^{\mathrm{axis}} T_{s,\zeta}^{\mathrm{axis}}}{\sum_s \sum_\zeta n_{s,\zeta}^{\mathrm{axis}}}
$$

where $s$ labels ion species, $\zeta$ labels charge state,
$n_{s,\zeta}^{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the local number density of that species
and charge state at the magnetic axis, and $T_{s,\zeta}^{\mathrm{axis}}$ is
its local temperature at the magnetic axis. The sums include the same
thermal ion populations in the numerator and denominator.

This is a local on-axis quantity, not a volume average and not the
temperature of a single species unless the included ion population is
effectively single-component or all included components have the same
temperature. It is the magnetic-axis counterpart of [total ion
temperature](name:total_ion_temperature) and is distinct from
[volume-averaged total ion
temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature). It excludes
electrons, neutral particles, and nonthermal energetic-ion components that
are not part of the thermal ion population, and it does not imply the
maximum ion temperature in the plasma.

items.name: perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude
items.description:
Perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the phase-independent
magnitude of a fluctuating electrostatic-potential perturbation represented
as a complex quantity. It is the modulus of the perturbation and excludes
the arbitrary complex phase.
items.documentation:
Perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude is the phase-independent
magnitude associated with an electrostatic-potential fluctuation. It
represents the strength of the scalar perturbation after removal of the
arbitrary complex phase of a complex perturbation representation.

The amplitude is defined by the complex modulus of the perturbation:

$$
A_{\tilde{\Phi}} = \left|\tilde{\Phi}\right|
$$

where $A_{\tilde{\Phi}}$ is the perturbed electrostatic potential amplitude,
$\tilde{\Phi}$ is the complex electrostatic-potential perturbation, and
$|\cdot|$ denotes the complex modulus.

This quantity applies to electrostatic-potential fluctuations in turbulence
for the perturbation variable being represented. No aggregation over
species, modes, times, or spatial regions is implied by the name.

It is distinct from the complex perturbation itself, from the complex phase
of that perturbation, and from amplitudes of other fluctuating fields. It
does not denote a vector component, vector magnitude, or vector projection;
electrostatic potential is a scalar field.

The [normalized perturbed electrostatic potential
amplitude](name:normalized_perturbed_electrostatic_potential_amplitude) is a
reference-scaled instance of this parent quantity: the same modulus
operation is applied to a normalized electrostatic-potential perturbation.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_passive_loop_element
items.description:
Vertical coordinate of a passive-loop element's geometry-defining point: the
geometric center in oblique geometry or a specified endpoint in thick-line
geometry, expressed as signed height in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of a point associated with a passive-loop element is its
signed position along the symmetry axis. It gives the geometric-center
height for oblique geometry and the height of the specified endpoint for
thick-line geometry.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate. The [vertical
direction] is parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis, and the coordinate is
defined by its projection:

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the point's position vector relative to the coordinate
origin and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis
toward increasing $Z$.

The coordinate applies to the geometry-defining point for an individual
passive-loop element; it is not an aggregate across elements. For thick-line
geometry it refers to the specified endpoint, not the cross-sectional
geometric center or an average over the cross-section. It specifies a
location, not a transverse size such as the [thickness of the passive-loop
element](name:thickness_of_passive_loop_element).

Sign convention: Positive when the point lies in the $+Z$ direction from the
plane $Z=0$.

items.name: angular_width_of_bragg_crystal
items.description:
The Bragg diffraction angle of the crystal in an X-ray crystal spectrometer
channel, fixing the central X-ray wavelength selected for diffraction
according to Bragg's law.
items.documentation:
The Bragg angle $\theta_B$ is the angle between the incident X-ray beam and
the crystal lattice planes at which constructive interference produces
wavelength-selective Bragg diffraction. It is the primary parameter
governing the central wavelength of a measurement channel in an X-ray
crystal spectrometer.

The selected X-ray wavelength $\lambda$ is determined by Bragg's law:

$$
n\lambda = 2d\sin\theta_B
$$

where $n$ is a positive integer diffraction order and $d$ is the crystal
lattice plane spacing of the diffracting crystal. For a crystal with known
$d$-spacing, $\theta_B$ uniquely determines the central wavelength of the
spectral channel.

In X-ray crystal spectrometer systems used for fusion plasma diagnostics,
the Bragg angle is established by the geometric orientation of the crystal
relative to the plasma X-ray source and the detector. It is a key
configuration parameter for selecting specific resonance lines used in
impurity transport studies and ion temperature measurements via Doppler
line-broadening analysis. Complementary crystal geometry parameters include
the radius of curvature of the diffracting surface in the toroidal direction
and the [aperture radius of the crystal](name:radius_of_bragg_crystal),
while the physical transverse extent of the crystal along the first axis is
given by
[bragg_crystal_width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_bragg_crystal).

items.name: heat_flux
items.description:
Vector of plasma energy transport per unit area, whose projection through an
oriented surface gives the power crossing it through convective, conductive,
and turbulent channels.
items.documentation:
The heat-flux vector represents the net transport of plasma energy through
space, including convective, conductive, cross-field, field-aligned, and
fluctuation-driven contributions when included in the energy balance.
